Title: EY, Blackline Alliance to Automate Finance Processes for Indian Enterprises
Content:
EY and BlackLine have expanded their global strategic alliance to India primarily to offer finance process automation to businesses across a variety of sectors. The alliance will also help expand EY’s process automation capabilities and finance transformation services. These services are offered to Indian enterprises to improve their Finance and Accounting operations and help them govern and automate their risk processes better. Also, as part of the alliance, EY and BlackLine will help businesses automate previously manual processes and support digital finance transformations. Arguably, the pedigree of both the stakeholders in the alliance can hardly be doubted. EY is a big name globally in the assurance, tax, transaction and advisory services. Many large entities in the financial world and capital markets trust EY insights. On the other hand, Blackline’s cloud-based solutions transform Finance and Accounting by automating, centralizing and streamlining financial close operations, intercompany accounting processes and other key F&A processes for large and midsize organizations.  It enables its 2,800 + customers worldwide  to move beyond outdated processes and point solutions to a Continuous Accounting model, in which real-time automation, controls and period-end tasks are embedded within day-to-day activities. So what is the modus operandi of this strategic alliance? Apparently EY will help businesses streamline their enterprise business processes using BlackLine’s Continuous Accounting capabilities. The offering leverages emerging robotic process automation tools, traditional enterprise resource planning systems and the capabilities of BlackLine’s cloud platform to help businesses. As part of the alliance, EY will also provide its experience in data integration, finance and ERP technology and experience in tax and finance advisory to develop an end-to-end solution and a sustainable foundation for continuous improvement backed by BlackLine’s portfolio. Under the terms of the agreement, EY will provide its experience in data integration, finance and ERP technology and experience in audit, framework-as-a-service, tax, and finance advisory to develop an end-to-end solution and a sustainable foundation for continuous improvement. EY will also provide insights into product enhancements, alignment with EY digital transformation and intelligent automation initiatives and systems, integration, implementation and deployment support for BlackLine’s cloud-based portfolio. Commenting on the alliance, Kamalanand Nithianandan, Partner, Advisory Services, EY India said: “We live in the age of the digital organization wherein it is become a necessity for the finance function to automate error-prone manual processes. Together with BlackLine, EY will enable businesses to stay adaptable, insightful and cost effective offering a unique set of tools and modules including BlackLine’s ‘Smart Close’, that will help improve governance and transparency both within an organization and externally.” Added Sibjyoti Basu, National Leader – Alliance and Ecosystem at EY “Today, CFOs are at the center of driving performance improvement across businesses of all sizes. The EY and BlackLine alliance will help address CFOs’ challenges in the Indian market by increasing efficiency and performance in the finance function through the improvement and automation of critical finance operations like accounting, financial close, intercompany processing, reconciliations and tax management. The alliance will further help CFOs reduce cost and risk and free up resources to spend more time on financial planning and analysis, providing higher levels of insight to business decision-makers.” The offering from the alliance leverages emerging robotic process automation tools, traditional ERP systems and the capabilities of BlackLine’s cloud platform to help clients:
  • Automate manual-intensive finance and accounting processes for increased efficiency and a more predictable workload for finance professionals.
  • Continuously improve the quality and accuracy of reported financial information, and increase visibility and control over critical finance and accounting data.
  • Govern and automate the management of intercompany transactions and respond to increased regulatory scrutiny in this area.

Title: HDFC Bank to expand by 200 branches and 2000 employees in the North East
Content:
HDFC Bank has declared on November 13 that its headcount will be increased by 50 percent to 6000 employees in the North East regions of India in the coming 2-3 years in order to cater its network expansion plans.

HDFC Bank Executive Vice President Sandeep Kumar reportedly said that the lenders will hire around 1500 people by the next year in Assam as the bank has its plans to expand its business by having a hike in the number of its branches from 72 to 100 in the state.

According to sources, Kumar even suggested that North-east is important for their business and since they already have 136 branches spread across the region, they are planning to take this number to 200 in the next couple of years.

In order to meet the targets, the bank will hire more people in the coming years.

While currently HDFC has 4,000 staffers in the North-east on company rolls, next year it would get to 6,000 people in the region.

The lender, the senior official reportedly told while talking about Assam has 72 branches in the state currently and it would soon turn 100 by the end of the coming year.

It is on celebrating 15 years of its operation in Assam that Kumar suggested that HDFC Bank is growing its business at 24 percent in the statecompared to 14 percent growth which is being seen by the Banking Sector.

He also said that their credit-deposit ratio is at 103 percent and their total business exposure in the state is at Rs, 10,209.34 while the bank has reached to 18 lakh people out of which 15.5 lakh have been somehow or the other touched by various CSR activities, across Assam.

56 percent of its branches in Assam are in rural and semi-urban areas.

Title: Fin-tech firm Loanwalle.com invests Rs 50 Cr in Chennai
Content:
~Expands operations in Southern India with their first office in Chennai~

New Delhi based fin-tech start-up, Loanwalle.com that specializes in providing emergency loans at lightning speed to - salaried individuals today announced its expansion in Chennai, India. The company has administered Rs 50 crores, specifically for Chennai, as a key potential market.

Analysing the growth spurt in the online lending pattern obtained during the test launch phase in October last year, Loanwalle.com decided to enter Chennai. The market analysis results clearly depicted the need for instant loan services catered by the company.

As per their analysis, the recent estimate of the economy of the Chennai Metropolitan Area has ranged from US$79 to US$86 billion (PPP GDP) and is ranked as the third-highest by GDP per capita. Chennai has a major economic base dominated by software services, automobile, medical tourism, hardware manufacturing and financial services. Apart from these, the other important industries    include    petrochemicals,    textiles    and    apparels.    The Chennai Port and Ennore Port contribute massively to its importance. Moreover, Chennai possess a computerized stock exchange called the Madras Stock Exchange. Subsequently, the aforementioned reasons make the city a potential region for start- ups like Loanwalle.com

Sometimes a financial crunch can get really heavy on people. Although the amount required could be small, but the urgency of money is so immediate and urgent that the long queues and time consuming paperwork can cost someone a heavy loss. Catering to those strata of the society is Loanwalle.com.

The company caters to the salaried segment, by fulfilling their need for instant loans to cover emergency situations at home or outside. Being one of the largest industrial and commercial centres of South India; Chennai has a significantly large number of salaried employees and promises substantial potential for those looking for services offered by fin-tech start-ups.

Commenting on the growth prospects in Chennai Mr. Sachin Mittal, Founder, Loanwalle.com said, “Chennai is a very important market down south. Following the results of our market research, we analysed that the market has an unexplored potential for fintech services like ours, hence we decided to set up our operations here.”

Mr. Mittal further added, “We intend to invest 50 crores in the next fiscal year, especially in the southern market. Our services will also be available in Tier II and III districts of Chennai.”

The company uses data-driven algorithms to help people with instant loan requirements to meet emergency situations. It uses an advanced technology system to simplify loan application processes as well as the sanctioning process to allow loans to reach faster to the customer. The app underwrites loan using banks and CIBIL analyser, data in phone, text, social media connections to determine credit- worthiness.

Incorporated in the year 2018, Loanwalle.com already has offices in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kolkata and is speedily spreading its wings in the remaining parts of the country. The fintech start-up plans to grow by 200% by 2020.

Title: $1 Billion raised by ‘Paytm’-the Digital Payment platform
Content:
The Delhi-based Indian digital payment firm, Paytm reportedly announced on 25<sup>th</sup> of November, 2019 that the digital payment processor backed by SoftBank had raise a heavy up-sum in a new funding from multiple investors ranging from an already existing stakeholder SoftBank’s Vision Fund to China’s Ant Financial services, whereas the fundraising campaign had estimated the Indian leading online payment processor approximately at $16 billion.

Above all of this, though Paytm had not disclosed the financial terms of the deal still sources suggest that the Noida-based Fin-tech firm had managed to raise as little as $1 billion in its latest fundraising campaign.

Apart from this Paytm has also reportedly added that it is working towards the expansion of insurance, lending and stockbroking and planning to invest about $1.4 billion (INR 100 billion) by the next three years in a bid in order to bring in more users.

Amid mounting losses due to the growing competition in the online payments sector with no clear source of growth in the revenue, the fund raising by Paytm had been in talks since the beginning of this year. Paytm is trapped in a market share battle for digital payments with PhonPe and Google Pay. The UPI transactions have made once the market leader- Paytm fall behind.

Paytm is trying its level best to turn into a comprehensive financial service firm so that the margins can be improved but has intensely struggled to expand its payments bank and other businesses. According to sources Japan’s SoftBank is suggesting Paytm to arrange new revenue streams and accelerate its spending cut.

According to reports, Paytm had received its last funds amounting $300 million from Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway in September 2018, valuing the firm at $10 billion. This is reportedly the first major investment round since then. Nevertheless, this year has witnessed the company cashing out employee stock options at a $16 billion valuation.

Efforts of fundraising began earlier this year in order to raise close to $2 billion but the size of the round got trimmed in between the intense competition and huge losses in the digital payments segment. Title: Reshaping of the financial service spaces & its future opportunities in India.
Content: Ramesh Iyer, Vice Chairman & MD, Mahindra Finance gives insights in to how frontier technologies like AI, Blockchain & IoT are reshaping the financial services space in India and how well technology partner are willing to accept customer’s knowledge as the input for developing new technology while emphasizing working with partners in the technology space is going to be a must. Excerpts from the interview - How the breakthrough technologies like AI, Blockchain, intelligent automation and IoT are reshaping the financial services space in India? For long years, all of us have use the knowledge that we have and we have done what is required to be done and I am speaking more from a rural perspective. We have not possibly respected data as much but once you put in a proper AI process in place, it crunches all the data you have and come out with models with are very - very trend setting. I can give you one example: Let’s take our recovery trends.  We would have had similar customer behavior the last 25 years. Have we cracked when we do the future lending?  Possibly not, because we used our knowledge and not the data adequately. But with AI coming in, we are able to forecast the behavior of a consumer going forward and then be able to guide the team on the ground has to how and what they should be doing. And we have done this and put to practice in our collections and I think that’s done a great job. Similarly, on the block chain : we’ve been talking about it for sometime but importance is how do you bring in that set of consumers who otherwise don’t get credit from the banking or the other system and  you have all the providers of credit on one side and you have  these kind of suppliers on one side. Once you get exposed to their ledgers correctly, I think the two works together and you can crack working capital needs of the consumers very well.  What are the opportunities IT channel partners have in the Fin-tech space? How can they address their customers’ financial requirements with the partnership with Fin-tech players? The whole space is going to work on a partnership approach. Gone are days where anybody can say that they will do it all by themselves.  Not from just the investment and cost perspective but even from the changing technology perspective, you need a technology partner who has the ability to keep bringing in the emerging and upcoming new technology. So, partnership is going to be a must. But the real requirement and what needs to be addressed is, how well are these partners willing to accept your knowledge as the input for developing new technology and I think their selection of partner will be very important but as I said, working with partners in the technology space is going to be a must. What are the future opportunities you see in the Fin-tech space in India? All these fin-techs are really  taking up our challenges that we have not been able to address as an organization and they do come out with some solutions but my concern around that is most of them come with a solutions for lending  but the  real challenge for a financial service is, how do you crack the recovery challenges. We will be willing to  put in lot of personal  efforts as an organization working with fin-techs and then helping them understand  the challenges from the recovery perspective and if they can come out with solutions. Fin-techs are here to stay they are the ones who help financial services crack multiple solutions and if cracked well can open up multiple opportunities.

Title: EarlySalary launches a new tool to check your Financial Wellness
Content: EarlySalary, India’s largest consumer lending application has recently announced the launch of its free monthly bureau credit score for its users. This feature not only will encourage them to make progress towards improving their financial health, but will also help them to work towards increasing their credit worthiness. India’s quick acceptance of fintech innovations in the past few years by millennials has made this feature an important credit-improving aid. According to the Credit Score Knowledge 2016 Consumer Survey, while a large majority of consumers know some basic facts aboutcredit scores, many of them do not understand the credit score details that have important cost implications. This feature aims to simplify credit reports for EarlySalary users, considering large percentage of their audience are new to the credit system. The credit score system offers a detailed snapshot of a person’s credit financial position, and helps them with tips on how to build their score and become loan-worthy. Another part of the product describes the historical score data which can be used to check a person’s score trends over that period and also analyse the factors affecting his score. A person’s credit score is determined by their credit card payment history, percentage of credit limit used, type of credit, late fee charges, loans active and various other factors. Apart from the credit report, the feature will also suggest suitable loan advisors and offers to earnest users. This will help users avoid pitfalls, further apply for loans judiciously and demonstrate stability in credit and financial matters. EarlySalary also plans to set up financial wellness seminars among corporates to help millennials improve their financial health. Akshay Mehrotra, Co-Founder and CEO of EarlySalary said, “Our data points suggest more advisory efforts are required to help millennials and young adultsto take control of their finances, and make smart monetary decisions to ensure a prosperous and stable future.Today over 10 Million customers have downloaded the EarlySalary app and more than 400 corporates have signed up for the Financial Wellness Offering and Salary Advances of EarlySalary.Encouraging them to sign up and check their credit score regularly, is a crucial first step in supporting them to understand their financial health and setting them on the right path towards making better financial decisions. To encourage growth in financial literacy and wellness, education and awareness programmes are important. We also have an on-groundeducation campaign with the same motive. We believesuch initiatives will go a long way to help people understand the intricacies of managing their credit well, and also play a useful role ininfluencing their financial wellness.” EarlySalary.com was founded by Akshay Mehrotra and Ashish Goyal in 2015 and is India’s largest consumer lending application, crossing the INR 2000 Crores disbursal mark. The mobile-first lending application has provided financial assistance to over 250,000 unique customers through 1 million cumulative loans across 17 cities, which has made EarlySalary the first line of credit for young working Indians.

Title: Commercial Banks Embracing Artificial Intelligence but Struggle to Use It for Competitive Impact, According to Genpact Research
Content:
Study shows 97% of commercial banks use AI, but most experimenting, with less than 20% extending its value across the enterprise

Enhancing customer experience critical to confront industry disruption

Nearly all (97%) commercial banks are using artificial intelligence (AI), according to new research from Genpact(NYSE: G), a global professional services firm focused on delivering digital transformation; however, most financial institutions are not implementing the technology effectively for competitive advantage.

More than half of the survey respondents (51%) are using AI simply for point solutions and individual tasks, with 27% testing in pilots, and only 19% leveraging it across the bank holistically. With pressures mounting from fintechs and other non-bank disruptors, these AI trials raise concerns about how effectively commercial banks can use the technology to improve customer experience (CX) and better compete.

Genpact’s study,Commercial Banking: The Customer Service Imperative, surveyed 500 senior commercial banking executives on the industry’s changing landscape. The research reveals that while many banks understand the growing importance of CX and AI, questions remain regarding their ability to use AI for greater value and mine data effectively to embrace digital transformation and enhance service.

The good news is most banks are optimistic about the future. Two-thirds of respondents say they expect to use AI across their organization in the next 12 to 18 months, compared with fewer than one in five today. Yet, some executives surveyed seem hesitant about whether AI will deliver on its promises to drive new personalized services to improve customer experience. Notably, 13% say their organizations have no plans to use AI in the next 12 to 18 months, up from 3% today, which may suggest a lack of confidence in current pilots and long-term execution.

“With digital technology opening new access to sales and payment data, non-traditional players have leapfrogged many established commercial banks in delivering quality customer experiences,” said Mark Sullivan, global business leader, Banking and Capital Markets, Genpact. “Banks must do a better job at anticipating and quickly incorporating CX innovations. AI can be a major driver given its ability to interpret droves of data to develop highly-tailored solutions that businesses want.”

 

Genpact’s research also looked fintechs’ impact on the commercial banking industry. Opinions are split: nearly half of the executives surveyed perceive fintechs as potential partners (cited by 56%), with others saying they are a competitive threat (44%). Most financial institutions are responding to this with a combination of competitive and adaptive measures. Genpact’s research shows many banks are ramping up their value propositions with enhanced customer experiences such as more responsive credit assessments.

Other commercial banks are unbundling their offerings and considering a “platform strategy” to provide customers with a channel for individual products in one place, including services provided by other companies. While “banking as a platform” may be effective to compete with fintechs, only 20% of respondents say they have a holistic strategy in place. And, just a little more than a third (35%) have mapped the customer journey across both treasury and lending product lines, which the study identifies as key growth areas.

“Our research shows that while leading commercial banks overwhelmingly see CX as a competitive advantage, many others are in danger of missing opportunities to build deeper customer relationships,” Sullivan said. “Few financial institutions are mining data effectively across products and other information sources to develop personalized services – which is exactly what fintechs and techfins deliver today.”

Genpact’s commercial banking research echoes similar findings in the company’s recent Banking in the Age of Instinctreport, which looks ahead to future trends in the industry. Commercial banks must connect the dots among data points and deliver more valuable insights to customers, a critical need for competitive growth.

Title: Only 13% of Finance Organizations UseArtificial Intelligence, Analytics, and Automation for Enterprise-wide Transformation, According to Genpact Research
Content:
Study shows senior executives understand benefits from advanced technologiesbut fail to deliver actionable insights from data

Business expectations of finance changing: enhancing customer and user experiencesnow top priority, ahead of costsand cash flow

Only 13% of finance executives are using artificial intelligence (AI), analytics, and automation to transform multiple processes across their enterprises, according to new research from Genpact(NYSE: G), a global professional services firm focused on delivering digital transformation.

Genpact’s global study,Finance and Accounting: Unleashing Transformation,surveyed more than 500 chief financial officers (CFOs)and other senior finance executives on business innovation issues. The research reveals that finance organizationsare well positioned to deliver strategic insights from theever-increasing amount of data that businessesmanage today; however, most finance teams are not fully implementing the advanced technologies necessaryto drive transformation for competitive growth.

When it comes to meeting business expectations to generate actionable insights from companydata, not a single survey respondent states that their function can do so significantly;58% say that finance just somewhat delivers insights.Moreover, none of the executives say they have a structured way to generate predictive insights to meet businesses’changing and varied demands.None also areusing AI, analytics, and automation to fundamentally reimagine their finance function.

“Finance organizations can be critical transformation engines for their enterprises, but they’re currently not firing on all cylinders,”said Katie Stein, chief strategy officer and global business leader, Enterprise Services, Genpact. “CFOs and their teams must champion the change necessary to drive innovation and compete effectively in a data-dominated and digital-first world.”

Genpact’s study reveals that customer experience is the number one corporate priority,ahead of increasing cash flow and driving revenue growth. This is reflected in businesses’ expectations from the finance functionin the next two years,where enhancing the experience for customers, suppliers, and employees comes out on top. While most survey respondents believe they are somewhat improving theseexperiences, only 1% say they are significantly meeting this expectation.

To support strategic business goals, the finance function must evolve to become the company’s enterprise data guardian. Genpact’s research demonstrates that finance organizations are making inroads, with nearly half (49%) agreeing this is their role, although only 7% strongly agree.

Despite, or perhaps even because of,technology-implementation issues, the executives surveyed recognize the importance of embracing AI, analytics, and automation when recruiting talent.The top two skillsets that finance organizations most urgently seek are knowledge of advanced digital technologiesand data-science skills, both of which top traditional finance and accounting capabilities.

“The need for new skills is clear – not just for finance operations alone, but more importantly, for the function to enable enterprise transformation,” said Stein. “CFOs and their teams can lead as strategic partners and provide faster, smarter access to critical data. The opportunity is there. It’s up to finance executives to implement digital technologiesand analytics more effectively, combining their domain expertise to deliver business insights that drive competitive growth.”

To learn more, visit Genpact’s website for the complete report,Finance and Accounting: Unleashing Transformation.

Title: RBI announces it's plan to launch a sovereign digital currency in India
Content:
The Reserve Bank of India on 5th December(Thursday) announces about its plan to launch its own digital currency. This  is reportedly the result of the ban on the banks from extending its services to crypto entities.

RBI expressed its seriousness in terms of launching a sovereign digital currency in the country. It assured its appropriate release sometime soon but its perspective on the ban of private cryptocurrency continues to be the same.

Shaktikanta Das, Governor, RBI reportedly stated that the issuance of cryptocurrency happens to be a sovereign mandate and since money laundering is a huge challenge, handing it over to a private company is definitely not an option.

He also added that RBI doesn't support any private digital currency in the country. Soon the bank has reportedly held internal meetings to discuss with the central banks for successfully launching India's own digital currency.

He added that the launch will certainly take sometime since the technology is in its initial stage.

The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) of July 2019 led by the Secretary of Department, Economic Affairs, Subhas Chandra Garg had reportedly submitted a report to the finance ministry on a ban on cryptocurrency in the country. The result was a recommendation by the committee suggesting the ban of all private cryptocurrency in India and the operation of digital currency issued by the government. The cryptocurrency start-ups are all stunned by this decision since this launch can get them out of business.

With this declaration many leading exchanges such as Coinome, Koinex, Zebpay had shut down their operations and other companies such as Unocoin had to fire half of its employees.

Also, a part of this declaration suggested not just the ban on cryptocurrency but also the proposal of 10 years jail term for anyone involved in exchanging, trading or selling cryptocurrencies in India.

Earlier reports have already suggested the desire in other BRICS countries to launch its own digital currency in order to have a fair competition with USD. Though any confirmation in this regard lacks but the buzz about India, China and Russia launching its own flat cryptocurrencies have been there for the past two years. Whereas Venezuela, Dubai and few other countries have already announced their  plans, India's plan on cryptocurrency have been running slow.

Nevertheless, the Indian Government has no plans to introduce the banning of cryptocurrency Bill in the Parliament in this year.

Title: Zetwork expands its operations overseas
Content:
A significantly large financial round has been closed by Zetwork, an Indian business-to-business marketplace for manufacturing items as it expands its operation in the country and simultaneously helps the local businesses in finding customers internationally.

The start-up which is merely 18-month-old reportedly stated that on Wednesday about $32 million has been raised in a series B financing round led by Lightspeed and Greenoaks Capital. About 14.2 million in debt from a consortium of banks and others have also been raised by the start-up, co-founder and chief executive Amit Acharya reportedly said.

Some others who participated in the round which pushes the start-up’ s total raise to date to about $41 million were existing investor Accel, Sequoia India as well as Kee Capital. Maninder Gulati, one of the top executives at Oyo, the budget lodging start-up and Vaibhav Gupta, Co-founder of business-to-business marketplace Udaan also participated.

It was last year when Zetwork was given birth by Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Acharya, Rahul Sharma and Vishal Choudhry. Connecting Original equipment manufacturers- OEM’s as well as Engineering procurement construction- EPC customers with manufacturing small-business and enterprises is what the start-up is responsible for.

Zetworks unlike any common e-commerce firms sells stuffs like parts of a crane, doors, chassis of different ladders and machines. Operations of this start-up deals with serving customers in the areas of machining, fabrication, casting and forging businesses. Zetwork at this point works with more than 100 enterprises and 1,500 Small medium-sized businesses.

As soon as a firm places an order Zetwork enables them to keep a track on the progress of manufacturing and thereafter its shipping. This kind of feature seems to be relevant in a business where the manufacturing and shipping business takes more than two-three months.

To help these manufacturing workshops by getting them clients online is indeed a new phenomenon in the country. The industry report suggests that manufacturing today holds about 14% of India’s GDP. What lacks is a support ecosystem in the nation to execute projects in a proper manner.

Vaibhav Agarwal, a partner at Lightspeed reportedly stated that it was quite surprising to come into terms with a marker that is as large as $40 billion to $60 billion in the country as well as global trade-tailwinds which creates opportunity to serve demands globally.

The start-up aims to utilise portions of the latest capital into expanding its operations overseas. Though Acharya didn’t give a clear view on the number of clients it has outside of India, but he stated that exports at present account for less than 5% of the start-ups gross merchandize Value.

He added that the start-up will keep focusing on helping the Indian manufacturers reach clients overseas since it is better suited to address this instead of helping Indian companies find manufacturers outside of India.

The start-up will further explore in terms of helping its manufacturing workshops access working capital, but this would take time.

Title: Mastercard launches ‘Identity Check’ feature to make digital transactions even more secure
Content:
In a bid to offer more secure banking options,Global Payments Technology company Mastercard launched an ‘Identity Check’ feature in partnership with Federal Bank for banks’ cardholders. Mastercard’s ‘Identity check’ is a special feature for authentication which makes the digital payments more secure using the latest authentication standards of EMV 3-D Secure. The increased security standards help in increasing the approval rates of digital transactions as well as improving the overall authentication experience for issuers, merchants and cardholders.

How Digital Payments becomes more secured with ‘Identity Check’

  The ‘Identity Check’ feature allows the banks to use a biometric solution for authentic cardholders which further helps to secure digital payments through strong two factor authentication. Through this solution the use of static passwords which are used in digital transactions gets replaced. A report suggests that the new tech and its insights allows customers to shop at any place of their choice easily. Irrespective of the platform, a customer can use the biometric authentication to complete the transaction. Whether its on a browser, an in-app purchase or through an IoT enabled device, it eliminates the need for entering OTPs or static passwords. Mastercard claims that the use of ‘Identity Check’ feature in other countries has resulted in the growth of digital transaction approvals close to 13%.

Smartphone to Become the next Point of Sale.

Mastercard has contributed with its share to push the digital transaction space in the country. The company has recently brough in a new technology in India in wherein a Smartphone can easily be used as a contactless acceptance device. The smartphone with near-field communication can become the point of sale device wherein a person can tap the contactless card in the phone to get the payments processed. This solution will be launched by Mastercard sometime soon in India, possibly next year. Mastercard aspires to double the contactless payment points to around 30 lakhs in the next couple of years. During this the company further claims to deploy contactless payment acceptance infrastructure in cinema halls, restaurants, coffee shops, supermarkets and petrol pumps where the ticket size is low. The company is reportedly also collaboration with the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT), acquirer banks as well as fintech companies in order to promote digital payments acceptance infrastructure an existence in the country.

Title: A workshop for the FinTech start-ups- IIM Sambalpur
Content:
Bhubaneshwar: A workshop for aspiring FinTech start-up was hosted by the Indian Institute of Management Sambalpur on Monday which involved key entrepreneurs and leaders from the FinTech sector.

The talks were about the entrepreneurial experience of the participants. They shared the challenges that they had to face and the mitigation methods adopted by them with the  audience consisting of Fintech Start-up members, researchers, academicians, students and business administrators.

The demonetization drive which got rolled out in 2016 could manage to put many start-ups in India's business map and consequently refine the fintech ecosystem. It was the ban on Rs. 500 and Rs. 1000 notes which removed 86.4 % of cash from India's economy. This therefore forced the people to switch to online transactions and digital payments.

This trend of digitization gave birth to more of digital payment platforms  and simultaneously the existing players moved on to achieve soaring valuations. The new fintech startups then somehow scrambled to take advantage of the opportunity as claimed by the participants. Not less than any boon to India's payment system, Demonetization led to three times surge with over 14 million new accounts, as reported by Paytm. Even daily users of Oxygen's wallet on an average increased by 167%.

Nevertheless the only thing to be concerned is security. The level of security, efficiency and confidence that banks provide is something that is expected out of the digital platforms too along with adequate laws  which can provide sufficient protection against any unlawful activities. Therefore the players in the fintech ecosystem while bringing forth such platforms must also double check the security factor since innumerable people are a part of this and their life can get heavily impacted with just one simple issue.

Title: HRtech start-up Salaryfits collaborates with Wishfin for its expansion in India
Content:
Salaryfits, A London based fintech and HRtech company has raised $5 million from Brazilian VC fund Confrapar for its expansion in India. The company already has its presence in Europe, Latin America and Asia. The start-up has also joined hands with an unnamed HRtech start-up along with fintech start-up Wishfin in India.

While discussing about its expansion plans in India Salaryfits’ Head of Operations in India Guilherme Mota reportedly declared that it has also formed a strategic partnership with Gurugram based HRTech player for bringing its technology and concept to more than a million of employees. Simultaneously Wishfin will be utilising Salaryfits technology to toll out innovative lending products from 2020.

Salaryfits which entered the Indian market three years ago has planned for its expansion in India because of the large unbanked population in India. Besides this India also has a growing number of “new to credit” (NTC) customers, who are young workers and digitally savvy entering the financial market. Salaryfits was founded by Renato Araujo in 2015.

Mota reportedly added that Salary-fits can get a successful model which promotes financial inclusion and easy access to financial products. He believes that empowerment o employees and financial benefits is still at a very nascent stage in India and he added that he is delighted to bring forward their thought leadership in India.

A grant of $1.3 Mn (EUR 1.25 Mn) was received by Salaryfits in 2016 from Portugal2020. The core audiences of Salaryfits are individuals who have just entered the financial market, those who have been ignored by major banks that are dependent on “inaccurate” risk management tools till now along with high levels of bureaucracy in the financial system. The company however claims that it will be able to bridge the gap between the financial institutions and these salaried individuals.

As far as India is concerned, Salaryfits is competing with start-ups like Quodeck, Talent Litmus, Vyre, Hush and others in the HRtech market.

Gamification for job assessment is not merely a craze. As suggested by PwC CEO Survey report 2018, more than 91% of business leaders believe that behavioural skills and technical skills are equally important. Title: There is ambiguity about crypto currency being a legal tender in India | Suryanath Tripathi | IIPA
Content: There is ambiguity about crypto currency being a legal tender in India |Suryanath Tripathi, Director, IIPA Crypto asset and crypto currency are no longer a matter of choice, as they are there and are flourishing. The question here is whether India as a sovereign country has accepted it or not. If not accepted, then what are the regulations, rules and procedures behind it? We are all aware that India has said that crypto currency is not a legal tender as of now, but we have also said in other Acts, in other provisions that if any profit is made out of crypto currency, the same is taxable which means there is ambiguity. Though the currency is not legal, but it is not illegal also. Suryanath Tripathi, Director, IIPA The second point is that state cannot be oblivious of the absence of revelation. Our IT Act prescribes certain activities of citizens which are valid and others which can be treated as a crime in absence of anything. Crypto currency is also a trading instrument digitally enabled, safe and secure, and if used for the right purpose, valid reasons and in the territory where it is accepted, the authorities will not say no. But the Government of India is very clear that this is not something where we will keep our eyes closed. Citizens are exposed to their data base, block chain and other technologies are there so nobody can say no to a technology. The only point is how we can use it for various purposes. Block chain we can use for our land record. There are many more things like health, banking behavior, trading behavior of all citizens. The legal background behind it is how nations are facing this menace of digital currencies because it is unregulated, nobody has tendered it, and therefore, how to fix the real value? Sometimes it would be half million INR for one bitcoin and sometimes it would be three-five thousand INR for one. It is very volatile and flexible and so one has to be very conscious while regulating it. It has to be regulated otherwise how a citizen will identify if something wrong happens. They have authorized that it has to be registered in stock exchanges which are approved by them, and cannot be run on own stock exchanges. The idea came from the fact that China has recently closed more than hundred stock exchanges which were trading these currencies. There are various examples available and we have to learn from each of them. Right now, smaller countries has used this as a tender document but bigger economies are still avoiding it.

Title: A CFO is at the center of a business organization and has to negotiate with all the business functions | Sanjay Banka | Merino India
Content: A CFO is at the center of a business organization and has to negotiate with all the business functions| Sanjay Banka, CFO, Merino India CXOTV.news caught up with Sanjay Banka, CFO, Merino India recently at CFO Network organized by Ezilone Marketing Solutions at Gurugram, wherein he has thrown light on the critical role of the CFOs and their contribution in driving business goals. Let’s watch the complete video to know what he suggests to be CFO of a successful organization - In our role as CFO we are at the center of the company. In terms of understanding the performance of various businesses, sales, marketing, IT and HR, a CFO is always at the center of the business and understands where the company is going because we have the numbers on daily basis as to what is the production happening, how much sales is happening, how is the manpower performing, and how is the IT performing. It helps us to drive the performance much easier and we do this by the way of deep insight of numbers and sharing those numbers and those performances with the functional heads, driving the strategy for those numbers and working and collaborating with the functional heads in their respective functional strategy. Sanjay Banka, CFO, Merino India For example, if we find the sales is particularly low on a particular day or on an aggregate basis is lower for the month, we understand in which region was the sales low, which was the branch where it was low, which = partner sales is lower, which product or which segment is selling less and then we compare that with the competitive information of my competitors working in the same area. We work with the functional head in understanding his original plan which he presented during the project and analyse whether he is able to perform as per the projection or if he requires more resources. This way we drive performance by understanding the functional number and supporting them, allocating capital to them, meeting their respective strategy. Let us understand the example of manpower. Manpower today is very critical to achieve the sales and the performance particularly for the yearly growth.  If sales is not happening we have to see whether the selling manpower requirement was for incremental sale or for routine sale. Then why the manpower has not been hired? Is it due to the recruitment agency not being on board or is it due to branding for which we are not able to attract employees. Hence we bring HR and marketing together and try to improve employee branding of the company and then attract the talent and ensure performance. So there are various tools and means through which we drive performance. Driving performance, one way is through the numbers. The second way is when you collaborate with functional heads in negotiation. So be it marketing contract, be it an HR contract, be it a raw material contract, we continuously collaborate with the business functions in negotiation understanding the function’s requirement, working closely with the procurement team, doing a proper product pricing, looking at compliance and risk as well, looking at three party courts, looking at GST compliance, look at the contract from their AMC perspective, post-performance contracts and so on. So you help the function get the maximum price which means get the maximum at the minimum. This way the company can perform much better. One more way of driving results is clearly industry bench marking and competitive bench marking. Any company should not work in silos; we must look at our performance and what the competition is doing. Now the competition data, can be available from the AMC website, from their own website and also there are several research organizations which provide the results. It is extremely important for us to get the data of our competitors at least on a quarterly basis, or if possible on a monthly basis to understand what the competition is doing, which product is performing well, what are the cost of goods sold, what is the GP margin, what is the interest cost? Once you understand which line item the competition is superior then you, then only you can come back with a better strategy and enhance the performance of your company.

Title: Moutusi Sau | Research Director | Vertical Industries | Gartner
Content:
“Banks need to adopt AI holistically; segmented approach would prevent them from scaling” CXOTV.news caught up with Moutusi Sau, Research Director -Vertical Industries, Gartner at its IT Symposium, 2019 at Goa where he shared valuable insights about
  1. Why are the AI business cases for BFSI industry different from others according to Gartner?
All industries have very different dynamics and very different drivers. What essentially moves banking or a banker would be very different from what a retailer is looking at. So, for banks one of the primary problems is probably fraud-- like how to stop frauds and similar bad events from happening. Whereas, for retail industry the main focus would be how to get that person inside the door. Therefore customer segmentation and selling would be one of the top priorities. The drivers of every industry are so different that you cannot really bucket them together. That is when = you can start talking about a laundry list of use cases if you start looking at individual industries. Within banking there are four business lines. There is retail banking, corporate banking, there is wealth management and capital market. Now when you start comparing a common mistake I have seen people make is when they call BFSI, they also include insurance in many cases whereas banking is very different from insurance. A banker would be interested in selling to a common person, whereas insurance is more interested in saving money. So for banks it is making money, whereas insurance is about saving money. And those drivers within all these different industries are very different.I am the key initiative for seven industries, namely banking, insurance, retail, telecom, manufacturing, healthcare, public sector.
  1. What are the challenges and bottlenecks for successful commercial deployments of AI in the BFSI sector? 
In the banking segment, one of the biggest issues is scaling. So, while doing the project successfully is good but scaling that project across the enterprise is the biggest factor that we are seeing. Just today itself, I heard a person complain that they already had a project in place but no one was adopting the project. And that goes down to the heart of why the projects are facing a roadblock. Because you need a big dataset at the end of the day for these algorithms to run and if folks do not use the AI project that is ongoing then the data would not be collected. So, in the banking segment I would say there is a big problem which is called the black box issue. Like how these algorithms are giving your decisions is not clearly described and that holds back a lot of this adoption.
  1. What should be the suggested roadmaps for CIOs to build business cases for AI especially in BFSI?
We tell them to start small, looking at some of the use cases that you can start deploying across the business lines. Take one typical use case, say a fraud analytics use case and start seeing how you can start applying that across everywhere. After that you have to put together a team which is called centre of excellence and you have to educate all of them how to get that across. Then it goes down to the vendor issue like you have to find out vendor who can do it. So there is a seven step program in the whole process of AI adoption. And essentially in the banking industry, following all the seven steps can get you to that scaling stage.
  1. Why Gartner has mentioned BankSight, Causality Link, Finn AI, Quantexa and Spotalpha as cool vendors in AI for Banking and Investment?
How we select good vendors is dependent on what is happening or what is hot that year. This year the hot topic was customer experience and we focused on that driver. The vendors that we selected had very cool applications on the customer site like how to engage a customer, how to start selling more. If you look at any of the vendors that we selected this year, all of them have proven their capabilities in the banks by using one of the use cases and scaling to that level. And they have also gathered a lot of interest from venture capitalists and they have gotten a lot of funding. But mostly why we looked at the reason the vendor would be a cool vendor this year was customer experience for banks.
  1. What would be the best practices for AI-based solutions in the capital market?
There is no one use case that can fall within the capital market. Capital market is actually one of the more advanced industries in terms of AI integration and capabilities. The most common one is trading. So they have use of machine learning for trading throughout. But I think the next good steps are forecasting & portfolio development. Robo advisory would also be part of capital markets essentially because it is wealth management.
  1. What would be your suggested roadmap in this domain?
I would again say because it is more advanced, you should be looking over to your peers for examples. There are firms like Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan who have been doing this very well. And they have established that using the equity trading space machine learning algorithms are very successful. So for firms who are still looking out for use cases look out to Goldman Sachs or JP Morgan and see what they are doing and then start probably copying some of those models into your own organization. But you have to also see what works for you and you have to look at your asset class, your capabilities maybe to some more vendor engagement issues. Maybe you have to find the right vendors for your organization.
  1. The common perception is that more AI adoption would cause greater automation leading to loss of human jobs. How would you rationalize the two in the Indian context?
From most of the data that we have acquired here at Gartner, we have seen that greater automation has not led to job losses but it has actually led to something called augmentation. Augmenting the human person is to enable them to do higher capacity work. So if you free up that person’s job by taking out the automated portion of his work, he could actually contribute more by being productive. And we did a work which is called business value where we have shown by data that actually it does not lead to job losses, but in turn it actually leads to more human augmentation.
  1. How would you predict the future adoption of AI in Indian BFSI? Will it be a fragmented approach or will it be a more holistic one?
Any AI adoption has to happen holistically as any time a work is done by segmentation, the adoption goes down. So in Indian BFSI as well the couple of very good examples that we have come across include Axis Bank having a chat bot that has done very well and ICICI having a very good holistic program. Any adoption that has to happen in the banking space has to happen via the entire organization development. I would definitely suggest the holistic way because segmentation would not scale it to the levels.

Title: Fintech solutions have reduced our turnaround time and improved our operational efficiency|Nitant Desai, CCO & CTO, PNB Housing Finance
Content: Fintech solutions have reduced our turnaround time and improved our operational efficiency|Nitant Desai, CCO & CTO, PNB Housing Finance Nitant Desai, CCO & CTO, PNB Housing Finance in an exclusive interaction with CXOTV.news revealed the company’s aggressive initiatives towards adopting fintech solutions and the benefits it is witnessing with the technology implementation for its Housing finance Excerpts from the interview -  Nitant Desai, CCO & CTO, PNB Housing Finance   How are you leveraging Fintech to grow your business and increase overall customer experience? We use fintech solutions right from business origination to the servicing of our end customers. This brings operational efficiency and enhances customer satisfaction and the customer experience as well. What are the Fintech solutions you have adopted? For acquisition, we have adopted solutions which integrate directly with players like Amazon, payers like Airtel Payment Bank and several other lead aggregators whereby the lead flows directly from them to us. In customer processing, we have used lots of e-KYC modules which brings efficiency in processing and enhancing the experience of underwriting and increase the efficiency of my underwriters. We also use Perfios which is a fintech solution related to analysis of bank statements. We also have a fintech based CRM which is completely digital, enhancing the customer’s experience while receiving the post disbursement service from us. What are the business areas and processes which you have transformed with Fintech? Service is something which cannot be copied otherwise all other fintech solutions can be copied by competition immediately. So what we aim is at giving a better service through our fintech solution. One of the biggest advantages we have derived out of implementing some of the fintech solutions is the deduction in total turnaround time while giving the approval to customers. We have also observed that operational efficiency of our processing staff members have increased multifold which is bringing results in financial terms whereby if a capacity of an underwriter was to process hundred cases, that has gone up to hundred and twenty five now. So increase in business does not necessarily amount to increase in manpower. What are your future plans for fintech adoption or expansion? We say for implementation of GST to appraise a self-employed customer in absence of finance or in absence of accurate finances, the GST related fintech solutions are going to become very handy to give approvals to our self-employed customers. Also the fintech solutions will help us to do complete paperless processing and paperless credit processing. However the disbursement process in housing finance will remain phygital till such time the land revenue records in our country do not get automated. What are the innovations in the technology transformation journey of PNB Housing Finance? The digital transformation journey of PNB Housing started in 2012. The basic requirement of the organization was to implement an infrastructure which is suitable for modern technology and so we implemented our ERP solution. We completely refurbished our infrastructure piece by 2015 when we completely implemented our ERP system, we had our network devices, our data center, our disaster recovery set, everything was ready and in place. We stabilized the system by 2016 and from 2016 onwards we started implementing on our digital journey. The first fintech or digital innovation that we did was collection on mobile; our recovery team carried a hand-held device which helped them to do a recovery on the site, collect the cheque or cash and that gets straight posted into the ERP system on time real-time basis. We introduced several innovative fintech solutions for our under writing colleagues. This is IBOX which helps you to do a de-duplication against fraud and also helps you verify the customer credential. How has these initiatives supported in fast track delivery of customer services? These initiatives certainly bring down the overall turnaround time for our customers while giving an approval or for disbursement. A process which takes about 15-20 days normally without any kind of a technical intervention is possible to turn around for a self-employed application in 4-5 days and a salaried one in 48 hours.

Title: Cleartax ensures compliance, security and improves your cash flow | Dev Ramane | ClearTax
Content:
Cleartax ensures compliance, security and improves your cash flow

Dev Ramnane,VP & Business Head, B2B Business at ClearTax in an exclusive conversation with CXOTV.news shares insights on how frontier technologies are disrupting the financial sector in India. Excerpts from the interview - How are breakthrough technologies like AI, Blockchain, intelligent automation and IoT are shaping the financial services space in India? Please talk about few use-cases where these technologies have transformed the financial business processes and overall customer experience. We have been using AI, Bot type technology to automate a lot of the repetitive task, even in our personal income tax filing. Today, we have a technology that can process any kind of form 16, which is your statement from your employer on your tax return or your employment statement. Automatically it can be read and within 7 minutes automatically all information in the form can be filled in. We use similar kind of technology even in GST. GST is a lot more dynamic as the law keeps changing especially for the larger businesses where the invoice volume is high. Now GST has mandated that you have to do an invoice level matching and if it does not happen and if the vendor is also not filing, you would be denied your input credit which indirectly impacts your cash flow. So, here again we are employing AI based technology to improve the level of matching as people make punching errors or there are date and month error. So we are trying to automate the function which an accountant or the finance people are doing. Dev Ramnane, VP & Business Head, B2B Business at ClearTax India We are even trying to solve issues like when you are trying to take credit on travel or hotel. From an audit stand point you need the invoice so our bots will go to various website, download it, create their statement and put it directly in the purchase register of the ERP. So there are various finance functions that we are looking to automate with the help of these technologies. What are the operational and financial benefits Fintech solutions like Cleartax offer to SMB and enterprise customers? Specifically cleartax offers three fold benefits.-One is, we try to ensure 100% compliance and reduce or eliminate the changes of any notices that will lead to lesser litigation on your tax. Secondly, we ensure that you can maximize your input tax credit in the most efficient and compliant manner so that it does not affect your cash flow. Third is that, we provide all of your compliance financial data in a very secure manner backed up for any audit or assessment so that any kind of query can be easily answered. Payments have been at the forefront of India’s Fintech revolution with UPI, mobile wallets, mobile banking growing aggressively. What are the emerging trends in the digital payments segment in India? The emerging trend in digital payment like UPI today is inter-operability. You can make payment in a secure manner directly from your mobile phone through various applications. I think payment is an instrument for doing many more things. Most companies are trying to understand how they can use your payment data as well as app usage frequency to provide various other utility apps to go beyond just making bill payment or recharges or making credit card payments. The growing trend is to explore how you can book a flight or cab directly from the app? Alternative lending is another space driving the Fintech story in India. What are the emerging business models and trends in the alternative lending segment? In alternative lending, the supply chain finance is one emerging area if you are dealing with larger company and you have an ongoing business with them, in order to serve or ensure the delivery on time. Now, if you need working capital loans, in the supply chain finance there is a concept called invoice discounting. This is where you already have an invoice that you have sent to a larger companies, they will give you early payment and the customer will get discount and the vendor instead of waiting for 60-90 days for payment will get immediate payment. This is one alternative way. The other is also looking at the GST data. Because GST has now access to all of the data, there will be some models that will emerge which would be looking at your flow of invoices and cash flow that is available through GST. That can give you a way to underwrite the customer in a better way and reduce the cost of underwriting, making it more accurate and reduce the NPAs also using the GST data. With the boom in digital transactions, the security of customers’ payment data has become extremely crucial. How are we securing the digital transactions and customer data? There are technology interventions that can be done for ensuring security. The data that is being exchanged can be encrypted,. You have a two factor authentication like when you log in to an app you get an OTP. In the applications available today like Paytm, Google pay where you have finger print, OTP, so that no one else can directly take your mobile phone and make a payment. These security best practices are already in place. What are the challenges that exist in the Fintech space in India? Broadly, we can see what is going on in the NBFC sector after the ILF&S issue. Investor confidence is a little low due to that in the alternate or NBFC kind of space. But overall this is just a transitionary thing. Fintech from larger companies to SMBs are going to use technology to reduce cost of operation, improve efficiency, and reach out to larger set of customer base. What are the future opportunities you see in the Fintech space in India? The opportunity itself is extremely large. You have a population who are still under served and not yet banked. So using mobile banking or app based financial services is a very cost effective and natural way to address a very large country like India. You take every type of financial services from banking to insurance to mutual funds to loans, all of these will have some technology or rather technology will help you to reach the customer better and serve them better. This can be done by the traditional players as well as there will be new entrants who will come and do it in a better way. What are the opportunities IT channel partners have in the Fintech space? How can they address their customers’ financial requirements in partnership with Fintech players? GST is a big opportunity, for company like cleartax. So basically now what would happen is that every ERP in this country will have to be ready for e-invoicing and e-way bills and they can partner companies like clear tax, so as to make their company GST ready.

Title: “India should not have crypto currencies for the next ten years” | Rajiv Saxena | National Informatics Centre
Content: In an exclusive video interaction Mr. Rajiv Saxena, Former Deputy General, National Informatics Centre shares his views on Crypto Assets and Crypto Currencies Regulation in India. CXO TV caught him up at International Conference on Cyberlaw, Cybercrime & Cybersecurity organised by Cyberlaws.Net & Pavan Duggal Associates on 20th to 22nd November, 2019.     Transcription of the video Interaction - I think in a country like India, the banning of crypto currencies for next ten years is a must. Right now, on a scale of maturity level, Bitcoin is the only cryptocurrency which has reached the second level of maturity. The total number of Bitcoins which can be mined is fixed. So, everyday computer scientists are mining newer cryptocurrencies. What happens as a result is that the value of all crypto currencies including bitcoins varies on a daily basis. As on today, the value of one Bitcoin is about $6000 which is a very high number. There are about 2000 to 3000 different crypto currencies but Bitcoin is very popular and most well known. What is happening now in the cyber World is that people are going into locking the systems remotely.  Now you do not browse the internet, rather the Internet browses you. And everything about you is known to five top tech companies of the world, i.e. Facebook, Google, Microsoft, Alibaba and Amazon. They know everything about you like what you do, your mobile number , email ID, when did you visit a particular store or when you had a surgery or when you visited your girlfriend and what you talked to your girlfriend and that is the most risky thing. They might therefore take inappropriate of the bitcoins lying with you. India is going to ban the trading of Bitcoins or other cyber currencies for the next ten years and that Bill will be presented in the current session of the Parliament. Money laundering is becoming a very important aspect. So, if we have black money with us, we may be able to convert that into a Bitcoin and keep it over there. For example, I have a Bitcoin and it is something like that cigarette smoking is banned in a complex but keeping a cigarette in your wallet is not banned. I may not trade my Bitcoin but I can keep a Bitcoin with me. You have to do the encryption with the private key which can be opened only by the public key and this way you can make many of the Bitcoins illegal and how? You hack the certifying authority which has issued the digital certificate and immediately what will happen that your digital signature will have no legal value over there which in turn will make your digital currency or Bitcoin become illegal entity.
