Title: Paul Merchants Charts IT Mission with New-Age Technologies
Content: While strengthening its IT infrastructure to make it future-ready, the company is modernizing its business applications by incorporating new-age technologies like AI/ML.     Paul Merchants is upping its ante on digital and security initiatives by leveraging new-age technologies like AI/ML, RPA, analytics and blockchain. The company credits its business continuity planning and existing IT infrastructure to help it easily sail through the COVID-19 pandemic and resulting lockdowns. “Going digital is no more a choice; it is the need of the hour due to ongoing circumstances. As part of our digital transformation initiatives, we are focused on modernizing business applications and explore low-code applications to make our business future-proof. In the process, we would utilize technologies like AI/ML, RPA, analytics and blockchain,” elaborated Shweta Srivastava, Chief Information Security Office, Paul Merchants Finance. Paul Merchants is one of the leading service providers of foreign exchange, international money transfer, tour and travel, business payment solutions, and gold loan services in India. The company has plans to launch a digital lending platform for which it will utilize AI and ML for credit assessment, risk management and fraud check by assessing customer documents. In addition, the company is plugging in bots with their online platforms and social media to connect with customers in order to aid its sales, marketing and customer service departments. “Blockchain is definitely the thing of future. However, we are still in process of exploring the use case for it, considering the huge investment in terms of technology adoption,” added Srivastava. Technology footprint Paul Merchants has been quite receptive to the latest technology trends and began its cloud journey in 2017 with all its business applications hosted on cloud, currently. The company has 24*7 network and security monitoring, PCP and DR systems. It has multiple digital platforms and mobile apps through which customers can connect and avail products and services. For instance, for foreign exchange it has www.pmlforexlive.com and a mobile app for Android users for online transactions through multiple choices like debit card, credit card, UPI, and net banking. For travel, it offers www.pmlholidays.com for flight and holiday bookings. Highlighting the company’s preparedness for any calamity including the ongoing pandemic, Srivastava mentioned that they keep analyzing the business continuity plans and perform DR drills regularly. “A real-life scenario like COVID-19 pandemic has helped us get the real value out of it. Considering the situation we are in, I think we've done a fantastic job and we've managed to overcome the challenges quite successfully.” She further stated that with the sudden lockdown the company was able to work remotely as it had all its business critical applications on cloud. “However, there was no way to connect to our customers, specifically, our gold loan customers. We never had an online platform through which the interest payment could be received. So in a matter of two days, we came up with the new platform through which they could login and check their outstanding balances and could make payments using the payment gateway.” The platform offers OTP authentication to verify the customer and to perform a secure transaction. The company is working closely with National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to launch its own RuPay card to increase the number of channels through which customers can transact with it.

Title: The best way to move on is to go digital: Anshul Srivastav, CIO, Federal Government-UAE
Content: Flexibility and digital transformation is the need of the hour for any organization these days. In this period of COVID-19 pandemic when everything is under the lockdown, there is no need to mention how difficult it becomes for the organizations to run their business smoothly, in every aspect. Even after the lift on the lockdown from some places, it is very difficult for them to work with different norms. No sector remained untouched from this deadly disaster. Anshul Srivastav, CIO, Federal Government-UAE, in an exclusive conversation with CXO TV spoke about how capable and flexible one needs to be in terms of identifying the right objects and elements required in setting up the infrastructure. Organizations have to be very clear about their business, what all components they require, and they shouldn't be rigid so that those processes set up that kind of capability around. If someone has to set up a branch somewhere in a remote corner of some part of the world they have to see the capabilities around. They need to put the checklist in place, get that checklist in order and see how they are going to connect that branch to the entire world. It is important that how people will be brought in, how they will manage to run the operations, backup of the operations, how resilient is the setup or the infrastructure and what is a fall back plan if that infrastructure collapses. Having such critical infrastructure it becomes salient for the leaders of the organization to take some major steps for the safe operations. And, hence when we talk of safety measures the role of CIO become prior. A lot of things to a great extent depends upon the CIO of the organization. From setting up the infrastructure to taking care of it the CIO has a very important role to play. Their role and responsibilities change as soon as the infrastructure starts changing. Digital technologies helping the businesses Discussing how COVID-19 is changing the fundamental business models of many organizations Anshul says, “Digital technologies which are helping the businesses right away are the ones which are something wherein human to human stuff has actually taken a back seat and more of the contactless piece has been considered more sane and divine.” “That's where we need to look at contactless payments, contactless deliveries. These are fundamentals and it hasn't gone down to the fundamentals of life in terms of the way you deal and treat people around in the business. So digital technologies have emerged so strongly and so profoundly that now gradually the processes which used to take a back seat in terms of getting digital, have to become digital because then they should not become a bottleneck for the business to move on. So, the best way to move on is to go digital,” he adds further. Technology solutions for client’s  Dealing with clients in such a situation becomes a critical task. How your customers or how your clients deal with you in future, because now the global clients would prefer not travelling and would prefer having it through zoom, Google meets or teams, whichever tool that would become a new normal. The customers who are going to be keen on your solutions would be keen on meeting you virtually and gradually the delivery of the product will take another shape of being more grown oriented coming in, more non-human being oriented deliveries happening.  IT policies will change drastically  “IT policies will completely go for reshaping, not only from the policy stack standpoint but also from the skills stack standpoint. The parent IT organization will have to reshape and reshaped in such a way that they work and can work from anywhere in the world. You don't have to be tied up to a location, you can work from your village, you can work from your small town and more IT policies should become on-demand policy, rather than you investing heavily on Capex. You invest in OPEX part of it. Uberization of IT will happen in a respective organization wherein more of on-demand IT applications and infrastructure would be required that would mean at any given point of time you know the IT cost and you know how to invest further in new technologies rather than everything on Capex and running it for years. So, your policies will change and with that comes another caveat of security. When things will go completely digital, the value of the security will take jumpstart and you need to secure your assets. You need to secure your data. You need to secure your ecosystem from your customers, partners, employees, and whosoever is your stakeholder” mentions the CIO speaking about their IT policies and SoPs in the current situation. According to him, “Security will take another level of evolution and the policies against the securities have to be redrafted, recrafted because everything gradually will tend to become virtual. And, if you haven't started working on being virtual then you'd be out of the market. Both security and regular policies have to be reshaped, made more demand, more OPEX oriented, were in the cost of your IT at a real-time level, rather than having a Capex investment and running that cost for over a period of four to five years with whatever is your depreciation cycle.” “The SoPs will change and SoPs will change in such a way that the on-demand will create, like I need a Java skill for two hours, so SoP for Java skill will be different. If I'm hiring a Java guy completely on the payroll and that SoP would be different. So, gradually the IT team would become virtual and more on-demand. The skills will become on-demand, the management might be on the payroll, but gradually I'm seeing CIO as service coming in very soon,” states Srivastav. Work from home requires a lot of protocols With work from home being a norm, would require a lot of protocols and security controls, which needs to be palmed in the security policies which gets injected through the network or the applications. It has to be controlled at a device level. It can't be exposed to the organization data or network with any number of devices. Now, with COVID-19 situation in place, people have a bit eased out setup, but have eased out a lot of their policies bypassing certain exceptions. For those exceptions, a solid risk assessment has to be done. If you see the evolution of workflow, the security teams and the IT teams have to work very closely with the risk management team, the HR team, the partner team, the sales team very closely and see how the emerging market models, business models are evolving and accordingly imply and comply the security policies within the organization. Remote collaboration technologies is a new normal On remote collaboration technologies being extensively used now the CIO describes that “they will definitely mature and would be more secured and more valuable to the organization in terms of remote working and remote collaboration with various functions. There is a tech part of it, and then there is a human part of it. Gradually the workforce who are not going to meet in person and work remotely globally, there has to be a kind of a way wherein this collaboration becomes more human and people would start loving working on remote collaboration technologies because when you are talking to the person on the other side, you don't know the person and so those remote collaboration technologies would become a new normal. That's how the world will evolve working with that because the world is not going to wait for another pandemic or any other major breakdown in the economy. The remote collaboration technology will become more profound, more mature, more secure, and much more valuable in terms of the growth of humans, as well as the world.” A proper security audit is a need of the hour In Anshul’s opinion, in the current situation, BCP (Business continuity planning) is much needed and it is more important to conduct a proper security audit of BCP. He says, “It's just not tech BCP, it's about how our people work remotely, how people manage things remotely. Especially in the sales side where they used to meet in person every time and how are they able to manage them converting the sales. BCP actually became more profound and saner at this point of time and doing a proper security audit definitely is a need of the hour because with the current situation, a lot of leakages in terms of exposure of data and exposure of setups, whether it's from the technology side or not from the offline side of the world, the exposure has been huge because you have to dilute your security policies to do business or to stay relevant.” Adding more to it he explains, “To stay relevant, you haven't compiled a lot of your compliances and the risk. You have to let go of a couple of risks because to be in the business you have to do it in a different way. So, a security audit is a must. Once things settle down and see where all those leakages are, where all those gaps are and how to fix it plug with the emergence of the evolving market landscape, you need to configure yourself to make sure those BCP audit controls are in place. Your business is not affected and the way a market landscape evolves you have to put controls. By futuristic security audit, you can manage the business and continue with the business and it is the essence of BCP.

Title: We are always ahead with the new future technologies: Sachin Lokhande, CIO & VP-IT, Pay Point, India
Content: As we know post COVID-19 crisis we have moved more towards a digital platform. For our day to day need also we are now depending on digital platforms. We do our best to maintain our physical distance and keep ourselves safe. With the increase in online shopping and to keep ourselves safe we prefer to pay online rather than paying in cash to a person. Hence the role of online payment platforms become vital as now it is used more. One of the important players in the genre is Pay Point. Pay Point is a versatile player in BFSI and travel domain and has a wallet system service. They have domestic money transfers, insurance loan landings, AEPS where the thumb impression acts as ATM/debit card. Sachin Lokhande, CIO & VP-IT, Pay Point, India in a conversation with CXO TV, talks about the company’s strategies, their security system and how it is different from another player in the market.  It's all about the services and targeted audience Talking about the market proposition and service levels to maximise business performance Sachin says,” It's all about your services and the targeted audience. Which target audience you are catering to and what kind of business model you are operating to is important. It's also based upon completely demand and supply. If you're proving supply to the end customer, I don't think there will be any challenge in this market. As of now, everybody is going digital.  Unique from other players in the market “We are moving ahead with the digital transformation and we are giving a complete digital service where people or end customer can definitely avail the facility to digital medium only, “says the CIO. “All over India, we have almost 65,000 digital channel and we are running a very different model. In the retail network channel, people and customers are getting various kind of services,” he adds.  Automation plays a vital role As per Lokhande, they are very much innovative and completely depend on technology innovations. They are adopting most of the latest technologies like automation, data mining, and data science. Also, the company is completely based on the RPA model where the user gets a seamless journey. So, automation plays a major key role in their future vision.  How do you ensure regulatory adherence? “We are having a very intelligent system and the back end where people get complete knowledge about the transactions. We have built a mechanism where the customer gets auto alert if anything goes wrong. Also, the system automatically alerts the customer when service is not available. We totally follow all the RBI rules and compliance and we completely follow the compliance mechanism, where we use to do a minimal human intervention and everything is automated,” Lokhande explains.  DMT & travel was majorly effected from COVID-19  According to Sachin,”PayPoint always follow a different kind of diversification area and we have more than 10 to 15 services under one brand. DMT & travel was the majorly affected by COVID-19 crisis. But, we have other areas working well like AEPS. Recently the government has announced that crediting money to people’s accounts and that can be done through AEPS. People are using it because we have 65K retail network channels. We are generating business from another source of the diversified area.”  Protection of asset “We always think positively and vigilantly based on the situation. As of now, we don't find any difficulties. We are focusing on doing complete automation to satisfy user IQ level. We are planning to design our system, according to the customer behaviour pattern,” mentions Sachin. Always ahead with new future technologies “We are always ahead with new future technologies and new future technology ideas. We are doing very well and there are no layoffs in the company. Everybody is working with us. No cut down in salary too. Everything is going well because we have taken completely precautionary actions. We have managed our expenses, expenditure, inflows and outflows in such a manner that we won’t face any kind of financial problem,” Sachin states.  Targeting 150- 180 per cent growth “When the COVID-19 crisis is over, we'll get a good grip in the market. The migrants moved will come back. Once they are back the workflow will definitely move more than 200 and 300%. When the situation is under control and we move further we'll definitely get 150-180 per cent growth,” says the CIO.

Title: CISOs & CIOs should always be prepared for the vulnerability: Deepak Kalambkar | AVP Infrastructure & CSO | SafexPay
Content: Online payment is a need for us these days rather than an option. To maintain the physical distance because of this far-reaching COVID-19 disease we avoid dealing with cash and go for online payment. All the digital payment platforms are doing their best to provide unrestricted service. As we know that these sorts of platforms are more vulnerable, so they are transforming themselves digitally to maintain their smooth flow with complete security. “Digital transformation is the key and will continue to be. Especially, post-COVID-19 it has been accelerated, that’s why we are encouraging working from home now,” says Deepak Kalambkar, AVP Infrastructure & CSO, SafexPay, in interaction with CXO TV.   Risks with online Payment  As per Deepak,” the risk in online payments has increased. In the current situation, 90% of people are doing the digital transaction, while saving their phone numbers, passwords on their mobiles. “Previously, the options were less. The payment was mostly done through net banking or banks only. Now there are wallets where they give discounts also. A large number of people are adapting to online payments. Online payment has reached across all the community,” explains the CSO.  Maintaining security  “Now we need to give remote work from home access to all our employee. As a CISO, I need to take care of security so, in our office, we have done VPN with multifactor authentication, RDP connections through a firewall where people have to enter user name and details. They'll get a google authenticator and then only they'll get access to our office network. We have taken all the security measures where employees can work from home efficiently,” Deepak states. “Post lockdown we have created VPNs, RDPs, MFAs and as per the employee's role. A separate VPN network is created for all group of employees. From last four months we are working from home without any security breach,” he adds.  The checklist  “Majorly in remote working, my checklist was VPNs to get MFAs, RDPs needed to be mapped with their IP firewall. The locks were changed by the security manager and infra person regularly and whosoever is logging in and out must be monitored,” says Deepak. All the employees can connect to the cloud and continue working from home as there's multi-factor authentication.  Providing white label payment gateway solution Speaking about their uniqueness Deepak says, “our company is the only company who provides white-label payment gateway solution in which we give the customer his branding on the page.”  CISOs & CIOs should always be prepared According to Deepak CISOs & CIOs should always be prepared for the vulnerability. In the present crisis, we have to fight for VPN connections and firewall protection. He thinks that a fixed IT budget should be there for such unprecedented times.  Better to move on cloud  “I'd like to advise organizations to move on the cloud. It is not that costly. There we can do data analytics also, lock finding is easy, and employees can be trained on the cloud very easily. We can also get multiple log-ins for them with MFA. There's data security and you can be mobile on cloud and any device can be connected to the servers as well,” suggests the CSO.

Title: Finin: COVID19 Crisis A Great Opportunity for Neo-Banks
Content:
Finin claims to be India's first direct consumer digitized bank that eases the customer money management, investment, savings account through digital mode using advanced AI driven technology and payment programs. Suman Gandham, Founder & CEO, Finin - The Future of Banking explains how neo banks are changing wealth management in India. What are the solutions and services that Finin offers? Finin is a fully digitized neo bank that provides banking solutions to their customers. We are a Neo-Bank, which focuses on the betterment of people, as well as enhance their Lifestyle. Our goal is to create hyper personalized banking solution, which help people to manage, save and invest their finances in a smarter, seamless way. Finin’s advanced AI driven technology analyze and tap customer experience and guide them towards saving, Investing and managing their wealth accordingly. We educate people to be wise in utilizing their wealth, which no other traditional bank offers. We are building our own debit card, which is at par with any other credit card offers. It contains tremendous offer for the customers. What was the story behind the genesis of Finin? While the Indian banking system has transformed in the past few decades, with banking becoming digitised and accessible, it was still not simple. Banking institutions had yet to serve the young audience in a way that made banking more convenient and make money management simpler and smarter. Finin took this opportunity to address this gap by creating a digitally-native banking application that provides a simpler perspective to banking using data-driven insights on spending behaviour and AI-driven recommendations help users to manage their money in a smart and efficient manner. We help you lead a financially-disciplined life while providing you with a delightful experience. What is the GTM model Finin follows for the India market? We are creating communities and ambassadors to onboard our customers. We are focusing a lot on creating financial education content, influencer marketing and also partnering with B2B companies to onboard our customers. We are building a debit card on par as a credit card with exciting incentives and innovative features. What were the factors that accelerated the growth of neobanks in India? The global neobank market was worth $18.6 billion in 2018 and is expected to accelerate at a CAGR of around 46.5% between 2019 and 2026, generating around $394.6 billion by 2026. It is due to some factors such as, Low Cost Structure: No Monthly fees & No withdrawal cost Debit Card Offers: Free Debit Card and tremendous offers on the same with global reach towards ATM. 24x 7 Support: The most important factor that can accelerate the growth of Neo-Banks is Fully digitized and 24x7 support from the same via chatbot, call centres etc. How will this get accelerated or slowed in a post COVID19 scenario? Covid-19 has a great impact on the world. There are many industries/sectors that have been affected by the same. The question is, which sectors are least impacted due to the pandemic. I believe digital payment sector is among the least impacted segments across the globe. Neo-bank industry being a very new concept and has many challenges to cope up with. I believe neo-bank industry is seeing every aspect positively and the problems that can be solved by them. One of the major problems that can be solved by Neo-Banks like us is wealth Management, “How neo-banks can help people to manage their wealth amidst the economy slowdown”. So, this covid-19 crisis can be a great opportunity for Neo-banks to prove themselves and come up with easier solutions to enhance one’s lifestyle.This pandemic really changed the perception of going to a bank and everyone are looking in to contact-less, no branch onboarding where are Neo Banks like Finin are already way ahead in paperless account opening and using AI extensively on the customer support front too. How critical role will digital payments start to play now in a post COVID19 world? As said earlier, Neo-Bank can play a very important role post covid-19 crisis. It’s not a secret that whole world’s economy can be in a great crisis due the pandemic. One of the major roles Neo-Bank can play is making people wise in utilizing their wealth. There are many ways in whichneo-banks can play a critical role post covid-19. What are the advantages/benefits of a consumer centric neobank like Finin in the current situation? There are various benefits such as
  • 24x7 availability
  • High security Features
  • International Payments by Interbank rate or less
  • Simple engaging mobile experience
  • Mutual Fund/Investments Advices
  • Debit Card (metal material)
  • Personalized offers, cash back and discounts, etc
  • AI powered smart budgeting
  • Goal based savings
  • Smart wealth management.
  • AI powered Customer Support
  • 3 min paperless online account opening
What are your key differentiators over other fintech competitors? Currently, there are no consumer-focused Neobanks out there in the market. While there are few competitors who are working on similar products, I see competition as a good thing as it validates what you are working on How much automation you can do with customer services? We are building an AI powered customer support system where a customer can get a solution to their issues even without reaching any support team. It is our magic sauce and you have to experience it. Who are your marquee clients and what are their use cases? At present there are 10,000 customers already registered and more to come post lockdown. We are mainly B2C, targeting customers from various segments such as College students, white collar employees and freelancers etc. With the changing dynamics due to the CIOVID19 impact, how are you revising on these plans? I think this pandemic changed the way people think about physical interaction and managing their finances. We are improving our features and solutions, which will make an impact post covid19 scenario How do you ensure the security of the model that you operate on? Finin uses bank-level security to protect your sensitive information and prevent unauthorized use. We have partnered with Banks that helps us with the transacted money to be in a much secured manner and customer can withdraw it without any inconvenience being caused. How are you looking at customer retention vs customer acquisition in the current scenario? Everyone say that Indian consumers are price sensitive but I say that Indian consumers are value sensitive. We are building our product in such a way that consumers can see the value we bring to them and their finances.

Title: FSS Payment Gateway Activates‘Pays’to Boost Online Sales
Content: With Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay merchants can now offer wider payments options to their customers FSS (Financial Software and Systems), a global leader in payment products and payment processor, announced its e-Commerce Payment Gatewayhas been enhanced  to support leading payment wallets  -- Apple Pay, Samsung Pay and Google Pay -- for online, in-app and mobile purchases.  The addition of new digital instrumentsis designed to help merchants meet evolving needs of customers for new ways topay andto boost online sales. Mobile retail commerce sales by 2023, according to industry reports, would account for an approximate 52% of total online sales. The recent enhancements help acquirers take advantage of this trend andboost conversions at checkout via delivery of effortless payment experiences. Customersmerely select their preferred Wallet at checkout, enter a biometric imprint or PIN, and the payment is done. There are no input-intensive forms to fill in or fumbling for a plastic card to enter the account number, card expiration, and security code. Commenting on the enhanced capabilities,N Sathish, Dy Chief Product OfficerFSSsaid; “The support for added payment instruments is timely as more merchants and consumers are adopting online payments due to the C-19 induced lockdown in most countries. The enhancements are in line with our objective to globally expand our white-label Payment Gateway footprint by bringing relevant innovations that delivers satisfactory, fulfilling payment experiences.” “We are thankful for the support from Apple Pay, Samsung Pay and Google Pay to help us bring safe, simple, and widely popular payment acceptance modes to the market;” added Sathish. For acquirers, setting up wallets for payment acceptance is a seamless process and takes a few minutes. The wallets can be integrated directly onto the merchant’s mobile website using a SDK or their desktop website. Whilst existing merchants have to opt-in for activation, with just a few lines of code, new merchants can quickly integrate the Wallet into their checkout process, allowing customers to transact in a familiar way at their favorite merchants. Alternately acquirers can use a white-labeled, out-of-the-box checkout hosted on the FSS Payment Gateway for wallet payment acceptance, benefitting smaller merchants who lack technical expertise. In addition to the Pays, the Gateway supports a breadth of alternate payment mechanisms including MADA (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s payment scheme), OmanNet (network for processing debit cards in Oman) Amazon Pay, Unified Payment Interface (India’s Instant payments scheme)to boost conversions at checkout. FSS Payment Gateway supports 70 merchant acquiring institutionsglobally and processes 1 Billion transaction annually. Acquirers can deploy FSS Payment Gateway in-premise or opt for an “As-a Service” model, wherein FSS hosts the service on FSSNeT (FSS private cloud) and assumes responsibility for set-up, security, regulatory compliance, maintenance, and regular product updates.

Title: Equisoft’s Integrated Digital Solutions Bridge Social Distancing in Wealth Management
Content:
Rana Biswas, Vice President - Insurance & Wealth Solutions, APAC, Equisoft talks through the solutions and business models and how they help in the pandemic situation.   What are the solutions and services in the Equisoft portfolio?   Founded in 1994, Equisoft is a global provider of advanced digital solutions in life insurance and wealth management. Recognized as a valued partner by over 50 of the world’s leading financial institutions in 15 countries, Equisoft offers front-end applications, back-office services and data migration expertise.   The products include a SaaS policy administration solution, CRM, financial needs analysis, asset allocation, quotes and illustrations, electronic application, agency management systems, as well as customer, agent and broker portals. Equisoft is also one of Oracle’s largest and most experienced reseller and integration partners for the Oracle Insurance Policy Administration platform.   Equisoft’s end-to-end insurance and wealth management solutions are designed to modernize every part of an organization to enable the company and its customers to thrive. For life insurers Equisoft provides integrated or modular, front and back end systems for both manufacturers & distributors. Equisoft is one of the world’s leading integrators of Oracle's Insurance Policy Administration system and has unparalleled data migration capabilities. In the wealth industry we deliver wealth management applications and tools for every end of the value chain, from fund manufacturers and broker dealers, to advisors.   How does Equisoft leverage digital tools around AI and analytics to grow its business further?   Equisoft’s digital advisor and customer tools are designed to help financial institutions streamline processes, enhance the advisor and client experience, and increase sales. Our software is used by thousands of insurance and wealth professionals worldwide to accelerate growth, streamline operations, improve efficiency, and grow sales.   The solutions primarily help perform five functions.  
  • Empower theRelationship Managers with data driven intelligence and fund positioning tools.
  • Build persuasive wealth plans for clients and efficiently manage new or existing relationships.
  • Strengthen distribution network by providing access to premium asset allocation and wealth analysis software.
  • Equisoft/analyze for wholesalers and Equisoft/analyze for advisors are all-In-one asset allocation and wealth planning tools for that increase efficiency, automate analysis, and generate reports, proposals, and recommendations, all in one place.
  • Equisoft/connect (CRM) and Equisoft/plan (FNA) enable an organization’s advisors to focus on managing customer relationships, not data. Our CRM software helps you spend less time maintaining data, and more time using it to effectively engage customers.
  How is Equisoft helping insurers bridge the social distancing gap with digital tools?   In a time of stringent social distancing, advisors can no longer meet face-to-face with clients. Clients can’t visit their local branch to make policy changes. This is an especially acute problem in India where the majority of sales are made in person. Integrated digital front-end solutions are required to bridge the social distance gap. Advisors need to be able to connect with clients remotely — and walk through a digital financial needs analysis (Equisoft/plan) and online illustrations (Equisoft/illustrate.) In order to remotely onboard customers, tools like Equisoft/apply (eApplications, eSignature capability), and online advisor and client service portals will become essential. How will insurance players look at technology to meet liquidity challenges or issues like NPAs in the current scenario?   Focus on Customer centricity using an advisor specific CRM solution like Equisoft/connect that enables advisors to easily be notified when existing customers are approaching renewal dates.  This allows advisors to engage those customers to facilitate collection of Renewal Premiums that will help retain persistency ratios of the carriers.   When interest rates remain low and insurers face liquidity challenges they need to find ways to increase efficiency and reduce costs. Modern PAS systems reduce the IT footprint, lowering resource needs and costs. Cloud-based SaaS models allow for lower, more flexible cost structures. System management, maintenance and upgrades are taken care of by the vendor. Modern PAS solutions accelerate innovation and enable insurers to more quickly introduce revised or even new products that are more competitive in a volatile market. Digital advisor and customer tools like illustrations and eApplications streamline the on-boarding process speeding up sales and reducing the per policy costs.   What are the new dynamics in business model of wealth management solutions post COVID19 pandemic?   Advisors, Relationship Managers and Brokers are now increasingly dependent on digital tools for Sales. Prospecting has now moved from phygital to fully digital. It’s now a virtual Face-to-Face prospecting and advisory. Both advisors and clients are now gradually adopting to this new normal.   COVID-19 has accelerated the need for change in the fund Relationship Manger’s role. The old product pitch approach to motivating advisors to offer a manufacturer’s products no longer works when advisors don’t want to and can’t meet. Instead Relationship Managers need to change their game – transforming into tech-enabled business consultants who add value to advisor practices. Equisoft/analyse for Relationship Managers allows them to offer a new portfolio analysis and design service to their advisors which enables advisors to get the most out of their client portfolios at a time of great volatility.   Insurance services were already digitized to a large extent before the pandemic. How did that help Equisoft to offset the business and economic impact to some extent?   The pandemic has exposed the vulnerability of the insurance carriers in terms ofthe difficulty of selling and supporting customers through digital processes. Across the value chain we have seen that insurance organizations were not prepared for the digital solutions required during and post pandemic. In these unprecedented times, connecting with customers digitally for all his/her requirements and providing seamless services is the differentiator. The carriers who are ahead in their digital readiness will reap benefits in the long run with their customer-centric approach. A robust and scalable IT platform is one of the big drivers of profitability for the carriers.   What are the Equisoft differentiators from other competing insurance and wealth management solutions?   Equisoft is globally used and locally supported—with the most clients in production   
  • 450+ Onshore Experts solving the toughest transformations
  • 55+ Financial institutions use our solutions globally
  • 35+ Insurance policy admin system integrations in the last few years.
  • 200+ Complex migrations of data and front-end tool implementations
  Equisoft is shaping the industry by solving organizations’ biggest challenges   The projects we have completed have built our reputation for tackling the toughest industry challenges, the most complex modernizations, and the most difficult data migrations. It’s what we thrive on.   What has been the traction of the Accelerate Series?   Response to the series has been tremendous. We have had well over a thousand key industry leaders register globally and attend the sessions to date. When the global pandemic broke out and conferences around the world were cancelled, we wanted to find a way to stay connected with the life insurance and wealth management communities.   We were very fortunate to have a fantastic network of partners to collaborate with, including clients,industry leaders, associations and top analysts – both as speakers, as well as helping to share the news aboutthis webinar series that was created to help executives navigatecritical issues caused by the pandemic, share learnings and positiontheir companies to thrive in the future. Each of the webinars have been live, and for those who could not attend the live sessions or missed them, they were recorded and are available as on-demand webcasts on our site. Given the enthusiasm from the industries, and all the positive feedback we have received to date, we’re happy to continue supporting this important dialogue and anticipate extending the Equisoft Accelerate Series into the fall.   How would you define Equisoft’s roadmap for the next 12-18 months?   We are very excited on the positive traction we have witnessed in the Indian market, both in the life insurance and wealth management side. We are in discussions with life carriers that are evaluating large IT transformation projects. Outside India, Equisoft is also positioning its insurance expertise in Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand and Bangladesh, while on the wealth management side, the focus is more on India and Singapore.

Title: Tenable advises to stay away from double-your-cryptocurrency giveaways
Content:
Comment from Satnam Narang, Staff Research Engineer at Tenable

“Several notable Twitter accounts in the cryptocurrency space have seemingly been hacked in a mass coordinated attack, including exchanges like @Coinbase, @Binance, @Gemini, @KuCoin, @Bitfinex, CEOs and founders like @CZ_Binance, @JustinSunTron, @SatoshiLite, cryptocurrency accounts like @TronFoundation, to promote a COVID-19 cryptocurrency giveaway scam. 

The accounts tweeted that they “partnered with” a company called CryptoForHealth. The domain for this website was registered on July 15. The website itself claims that, to help with the hard times endured by COVID-19, they’re partnering with several exchanges to provide a “5000 Bitcoin (BTC) giveaway” which is a ruse for advanced free fraud.

In separate but related attacks, the verified accounts of Bill Gates, Elon Musk and Uber were also compromised to promote a cryptocurrency giveaway. Their tweets used the same Bitcoin address we observed on the CryptoForHealth site, indicating that this is likely a coordinated attack.

The hackers ask users to send anywhere between 0.1 BTC to 20 BTC to a designated Bitcoin address and that they’ll double victims’ money. This is a common scam that has persisted for a few years now, where scammers will impersonate notable cryptocurrency figures or individuals. What makes this incident most notable, however, is that the scammers have managed to compromise the legitimate, notable Twitter accounts to launch their scams. Because the tweets originated from these verified accounts, the chances of users placing their trust in the CryptoForHealth website or the purported Bitcoin address is even greater. This is a fast moving target and so far over $50,000 (INR 3760940) has been received by the Bitcoin address featured on the CryptoForHealth website and in Elon and Bill Gates’ tweets. We strongly advise users never to participate in so-called giveaways or opportunities that claim to double your cryptocurrency because they’re almost always guaranteed to be a scam.”

Title: IndusInd Bank successfully completes integration with CRMNEXT across all its customer touch points
Content:
• IndusInd Bank adopts a smarter, faster and deeper customer engagement strategy with an agile technology platform
IndusInd Bank has announced its successful integration with CRMNEXT, the leading enterprise solution provider for banks and financial services. This integration will enable the Bank to simplify the process of customer on-boarding, introduce new products and meet customer demands by automating and customizing processes to fit the modern-day financial requirements.   The CRMNEXT platform will empower IndusInd Bank with an intelligence driven ‘Customer Action Center’ which will provide complete information on customers acquired from multiple sources, and make it available on a single intuitive screen. This will give the Bank a holistic view of customer relationships across product offerings, thereby enabling the Bank officials to build smarter relationship programs, and also initiate activities for faster sales and service fulfilment.   The platform will be implemented across IndusInd Bank’s wide network of nearly 2000 branches, call centers and processing units for sales and service operations. It will also integrate and power all  digital and physical banking touch points including ATMs, WhatsApp Banking platform, Email, SMS, Mobile apps etc. as well as over 150 integration touch points including core banking, loan systems, credit card system, Aadhaar, credit bureaus among others.   Speaking about the integration, Mr. Soumitra Sen, Head - Consumer Banking, IndusInd Bank, said, “Technology and innovation have always been a critical focus area for the bank and that has been key towards achieving customer satisfaction. In keeping with this vision, we are delighted to integrate our banking systems with the CRMNEXT platform which will help automate and personalize processes, so that we can focus on meeting the unique needs of every customer and be even more strongly able to deliver stellar user experiences across the board.”   Talking about the integration, Mr. Anil Rao, Head – Operations and Solution Delivery, IndusInd Bank, said, “Transitioning to a high impact digital platform has been a massive, yet seamless experience with CRMNEXT. It will help us to drive our digital strategies in an agile and scalable environment efficiently, with faster fulfilment, delivering superior customer experience. Building on the robust new customer management platform, we aim to cement our position as a digital first bank."   Mr. Biswabrata Chakravorty, Chief Information Officer, IndusInd Bank, said “The launch of the next generation CRM platform is in line with IndusInd Bank’s vision to transform to a Digital Bank focussed in providing best-in-class banking services enabled through innovative use of technology. The Bank has created a digital customer experience and action platform leveraging the elasticity and resilience of the Cloud and through a robust API led integration with all customer touch points.  This platform will provide a unified view of the customer across the lifecycle by incorporating the principle of a golden customer profile from lead/prospect to after sale service. This platform will be accessed by all customer facing channels and staff, making it challenging from a design point of view. IndusInd Bank has leveraged partnership with industry leading platforms like CRM Next, VmWare and Amazon to deliver on this ask and architected it for a seamless client experience.”   Mr. Sushil Tyagi, Director, CRMNEXT, said, "With the increasing influence of digital in customers’ everyday lives, it’s critical for banking institutions to deliver a delightful and consistent digital experience. CRMNEXT is the leader in digital customer experience platform for banks with an exemplary delivery track record, we are confident to further power IndusInd in its growth strategy bringing efficiencies with large scale optimization and smart automation."   Appended below, are some of the benefits of the integration with CRMNXT:
  • The integration will enable the Bank to anticipate customer needs well in advance,and craft personalized offerings, thereby enhancing customer loyalty.
  • Codeless, visual digital journey designers enable personalized sales, service offerings with significantly faster turn-around-time and lower operational costs.
  • Guided actions will help the teams at IndusInd Bank to curate their engagement activities, and build long term relationships with stakeholders.

Title: Innovation during the time of crisis and role of technology
Content:
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/IrbRG5qfxOk" width="560" height="315" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe>

Rachit Chawla | CEO | Finway explains how technology will help in the altered business model

We have a mobile application FLAP (Finway Loan Assists for Partners) which helped us save a lot of costs. We have a 1000 odd agents across India and we have a good distribution network. We have a lot of feet on the ground because of these agents but we do not have any fixed costs. The way it works is that our agents use the mobile app as the selling point where they educate the customers, take the customer orders andput the leads. Everything they do is through this virtual digital technology.

It is all proprietary owned by Finway have worked since last three years on it very extensively. Now it helps us. Our cost is always very low because it is variable in nature. So if a consumer buys a product, then only we share the commission with our agents. Secondly, during the time of crisis we were able to remain in touch with every single customer through that digital medium. We got to know as in what and when was the product they required, whether it was insurance, investments or loan. Every single update we automatically get from the consumers end because it is a very technology driven kind of a method that we use. That really helped us scale the operations also.

The crisis is huge because all of a sudden the productive policy of all of our partners, our institutions changed all of a sudden. Since we had to serve a larger consumer base, we further got in touch with other FinTech players who were doing good in B2B and the NBFCs who are not dealing in the same products as we are. We formed a cartel and we served the consumers digitally.

During Corona we cannot do any paperwork, because nobody wants to step out of their house, but the technology helped us serve our customer during that period. We were able to disburse loans to them, we were able to educate them about more and more innovative products and it also helped us sail through this difficult period in Delhi particularly. Not so much in Bombay because in Bombay certain parts are still in lockdown. In Delhi, we see people on the streets and getting back to business, but it is not the same case in other parts of India. It is only through technology that we can drive. Companies which did not have technology are shutting down because of the high costs involved otherwise.

Secondly, we believe in extensively training our agents and our team members. We have certain physical training places across India that are now shut down but people are using services like Zoom or virtual connectivity. What we have is an in-built mobile app framing institute where every day some product or the other is being taught to all the agents and team members. Whoever joins us gets that piece free of cost. COVID changed the entire product dynamics and in order to keep that product knowledge up to date, we came up with this innovative solution where every day somebody or the else is taking training sessions online.

We have added a lot of analytics and Big Data just to understand consumer behavior and foresee the changes in product dynamics. We saw in three months the product and underwriting process changed drastically. So what people should do is rather than relying heavily on manual intervention, they should have proprietary technology in-house, because technology is something that gives you data and data gives you truth. Irrespective of whatever people say, if your data says that consumers are happy, turn around time is good, and you are getting good feedback, that means your company is set to grow because data tells you the reality. So my suggestion to everybody is that they should definitely look at scaling up pan India digitally because the fragmentation will go with time. You will see a lot of people who are heavily invested in brick and mortar are already shutting down because it is not sustainable.
The market has become very competitive. Now in this competitive market consumers need to get complete value. How will you give consumers the complete value when you are burdened with a lot of costs? You need to reduce cost by leveraging technology and pass on the entire value chain to the consumer, only then you can grow. Rather than taking 1% out of Rs 1 crore revenue which is Rs 1 lakh, everybody should aim at a Rs 100 crore revenue and taking 0.1% which is Rs 10 lakh. I think that that should be the mindset and that is how I see the future shaping up.

Title: Market Outlook - July 2020 - Mr NavneetMunot, CIO, SBI Mutual Fund
Content: The June’20 quarter ended up being the best for US equities in over 20 years. Bouts of volatility are likely as the divergence between markets fundamentals and macro fundamentalsgetsaddressedwiththelattercatchingupalbeitmuchgradually.USM2growthisalreadyatamulti-decade high. The Fed has stayed dovish with respect to forward guidance. Expansionary fiscal policy is here to stay as we believe governments globally will resort to Keynesian economics to create low end jobs through infrastructure spending in the wake of rising inequality and socialpressures.   The combination of unprecedented monetary and fiscal stimulus globally should prove reflationary on the other side of the crisis. Markets believe that the worst on the economy is behind. However, the zigzag on the health crisis will likely continueinthenearterm.ContinuedriseinnumberofcasesinIndiaandinothercountriesincludingtheUSisconcerning. In addition, with a democraticset-up,ruleoflaw,andIPprotection,Indiaofferstrustandtransparency.Buildingstrengthontechnologymay take time, but data surely is a strength and through right execution we can forgeahead.   The right policy mix is critical. We need to create a robust ecosystem to nurture entrepreneurs. Start-ups in India have been funded by VCs or PEs that have largely relied on foreign money, as domestic investors have stayed away. We now boast of foreign exchange reserves in excess of US $500 billion. Time may have come to think about our own sovereign fund to fund innovation and provide the much-needed risk capital. Covid-19 is a similar inflection point in our journey, and we must make the most ofit.   The Covid-19 crisis is likely to accelerate deglobalization and localization in manufacturing, and at the same time lead to increased globalization on services. Both are trends that India is well placed to capitalize on. On manufacturing, we need togowithfullmight,throughpolicy,capitalandinfrastructuresupport,tohelpindustriesthat wewanttoprioritizeaswe   makeinIndia,andforIndia.Wehavebecomecompetitiveoncorporatetaxrate.WehavecreatedsuccessstoriesinAutos, Pharma, and Light industrials. However, we still have external dependenciesinboththatneedtobeaddressedandlocalizedtotheextentpossible.Bringingdownthecostoffactorsof production, a focus on innovation and a business-friendly environment are critical to realize our truepotential.   In contrast to the deglobalization narrative, services could actually witness more globalization owing to the Covid disruption. The west has many Indian doctors, professors, and tech professionals. Earlier they had to physically relocate afterobtainingaVisa.Todaywithincreasedvirtualization,theycanbemoreeasilyemployedwithouttheneedofphysical movement. More and more firms are adopting Work from Anywhere. What stops a teacher in India to impart education to kids in the US through a virtual classroom or a doctor to administer telemedicine to a patient anywhere. Title: NSDC and Airtel Payments Bank collaborate to create employment opportunities within the financial services industry
Content:
• Will co-create and conduct training programs on financial services for youth in rural areas to help them find job or entrepreneurship opportunity  
Airtel Payments Bank and National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) today announced a partnership to skill youth in rural India and enable them to find employment opportunities within the financial services industry.   Financial services, viz.banking, payments, insurance and allied services – are growing rapidly in the country and in particular, the underpenetrated markets comprising of villages and Tier 4/5/6 towns. These services present a massive opportunity in tandem with the Government’s vision for financial inclusion.Youth population coming from the emerging markets has the potential to be a part of this growth journey.   The partnership aims to combine NSDC’s rich experience,deep training infrastructure, and wide network with Airtel Payment Bank’s industry insights to design and conduct targeted skill development programs for rural youth.  
  • The Skill Development Programs will be tailored for imparting knowledge and skills for entry-level jobs such as Business Correspondent, Field Sales Executive, etc among others within the financial services sector. There will be a strong focus on adoption of digital tools to drive online banking and digital financial services given the growing penetration of affordable smartphones and 4G networks in the country.
 
  • Airtel Payments Bank and NSDC will leverage their industry linkages and help the participants in finding suitable jobs.
 
  • The partnership will also encourage skill trainees to become entrepreneurs, such as distributors/resellers of financial services, thereby creating employment opportunities for people in their local geographies.
  Further, Airtel Payments Bank will also conduct an awareness drive at NSDC’s training centres. Under this drive, the Bank will organize sessions highlighting importance of digital banking, its benefits and also provide hand on digital banking experience during these sessions.   This collaboration will also extend to Eskill India, NSDC’s digital skilling initiative. Special learning modules will be built to create awareness about digital financial service and will be introduced on the platform.   Commenting on the partnership, Dr. Manish Kumar, MD & CEO, NSDC said, “Financial inclusion empower people and promote ‘inclusive’ growth of the nation. Through our strategic partnership with Airtel Payments Bank, we aim at imparting the youth with knowledge and training that render financial and banking services more accessible to rural and semi-urban India.”     Mr. Anubrata Biswas, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Airtel Payments Bank, said, “India has the largest youth population in the world and a large proportion is residing in small towns and villages of the country. We believe they must become a key part of India’s growth journey and be able to fulfil their dreams and aspirations. We are delighted to partner with NSDC to empower our youth and build a financially inclusive India.”

Title: Bank of Baroda’s Credit Card Arm Readies for Digital Transformation with Implementation of Fiserv Technology
Content:
Flexible, scalable solution accelerates digital transformation of card issuing and processing

BOB Financial Solutions Limited (BFSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Bank of Baroda, has chosen Fiserv, Inc. (NASDAQ: FISV), a leading global provider of payments and financial services technology solutions, to enable the digitization of their end-to-end card issuance and processing cycle and support the launch of several new and high-tech products including contactless credit cards, tokenisation and integration with branded wallets, and virtual credit cards.   BFSL is one of the earliest issuers of credit cards in India and has a reputation for delivering superior card products and services to its customers. To advance their digital strategy and keep pace with rapidly changing consumer expectations, BFSL will utilize FirstVisionTM from Fiserv, an end-to-end managed services solution that enables card issuing and processing with global economies of scale and integrated capabilities that span the card lifecycle.   The service-oriented architecture and open APIs of FirstVision facilitate rapid application development, enabling new capabilities to be brought to market more quickly and at a lower cost. The software as a service (SaaS) solution is hosted locally in India and enables card processing for major issuers across the country, helping ensure compliance with local payment and customer data regulations.   “Delivering robust, secure products and a superior experience to our customers is our priority,” said Shailendra Singh, managing director and CEO at BOB Financial Solutions Limited. “Fiserv understands our market, and we value the fact that their card processing capabilities are hosted in India. The scalable, integrated technology provided by Fiserv will allow us to deliver the experiences our customers expect now and into the future, as we accelerate the launch of new products and services being adopted by all major issuers.”   The FirstVision platform will enable BFSL to move forward on their digital transformation journey with a fully integrated suite of card management tools including digital cards and loyalty management, advanced fraud modules, risk management and analytics solutions.   “The speed at which financial services providers need to satisfy customer demand for digital services has further accelerated as a result of the impact of COVID-19,” said Ivo Distelbrink, EVP and head of Asia Pacific at Fiserv. “With Fiserv, BFSL can reimagine customer journeys and launch to market with speed in order to better serve their customers in a rapidly changing digitally-centric world.”

Title: “We were maybe the first to move the Algo trading platform to a HCI mode”- Dr. Mukesh Mehta
Content: Dr. Mukesh Mehta |Chief Technology Officer | Batlivala & Karani Securities reveals how digitization helped him in the current situation. What are the key technology solutions used by Batlivala and Karani and what are their use cases? We are mainly using the trading platforms, which are vendor based applications. The operation part is managed by our team while the development is managed by the respective vendor. We have a back office and middle office also. Apart from the main trading platform, we have a complete research platform, which is developed completely in-house We are using lots of BI tools in our research automation. We really focus on our BI activities and most of my research automation is completely data driven and the support system is already on there. We have another vertical-- the mutual fund. We are one of India's top players in the mutual funds distributions for the corporate. The entire mutual fund platform is also in-house developed. I am a strong believer of in-house whether it is indevelopment, it is a data center, or whether it is our infrastructure managing the SOC and NOC also. You will have a very rare combination where everything is in house. How are digital technologies helping Batlivala and Karani to tide over the current COVID19 crisis? We immediately moved entire things to WFH culture, which was not our working style. Immediately within the first few days we had to move everybody, the desktops and laptops, everything to the respective user's home.Being the institutional dealer, the regulators do not allow you to have work from home for the dealings. And there are lots of other dependencies also because of the global markets. So the dealing team is already working in the office which we have split into team A and team B concept. The research automation, which we did last year in 2019 or late 2018,, has really helped us in this. We are getting the real fruits of that hard work. The same is with the mutual fund platform also, the business line also, where lot of things have been done, automation and everything., It is cloud based for that particular business. We never had 10 or 20+ people on the concurrent. All of a sudden I have 200 people on the VPN at any point of time. So the load of the VPN was re-tested and re-visited. That is where we moved on to lots of collaboration tools also, like Microsoft Teams. The digitization has really helped us a lot. How has the implementation of the hyper converged infrastructure (HCI) benefited the trading platform at Batlivala and Karani? I have a privilege to be one of the very few or maybe the CIO first in India to have the complete trading platform on the HCI, which includes Algorithm trading, HAP and other things. We moved our entire thing into HCI platform in late, 2017 or early 2018 . The platform has its own advantages. Scalability is the biggest thing and we are using the complete bouquet of HCI irrespective of the trading platform or the hybrid cloud which is becoming a part of my HCI activity. It is almost 4+ years, and the journey has been awesome and now with the airborne refresh and all those, infrastructure challenges are becoming almost zero. How has the prolonged WFH scenario changed the entire DR-BCP plans of organizations? Everything is working, everything is available there , but to drive the people, logistic challenges are still there. But on weekends, we are doing a real testing of the availability of the DR-BCP. As of now we are in control, but my biggest challenge continues to be more of the people rather than process or of the policies. Technology wise, we are available, we are ready. There is no process, but the logistic movement of the people will continue to be there. We upgraded our infrastructure on the DR site immediately, the link updates have already happened, couple of infrastructure changes has been made. My P2P links. Monthly mock sessions are there, and we are managing it.  How has Batlivala and Karani ensured increasing transparency through communication and collaboration solutions in the post pandemic period? From our traditional activities of phones and chats, we completely migrated to Microsoft Teams. So research morning meetings are now on Teams. Everybody is on teams. We had a very large investor conclave, which lasted for four days completely on a digital platform. So lots of things have happened and post the situation when we will back to the normal, we will continue to use Microsoft Teams and the other collaboration tools to ensure more productivity happen. There is huge cost savings also. So now we have realized that this is the way to work even when we are back to the old normal. This is going to continue at least for the next one or two years. Then time will tell how to revisit the entire thing. How can digital technologies help tide over liquidity crisis or NPA challenges? Digital technology has improved many things and it is bringing more and more transparency in the system. Irrespective of the NPAs or other business lines, digital is the way to go forward. And these situations actually push you more on those things irrespective of the liquidity crisis or impact of the financial market. The advantages of using these technologies are that we are able to trace everything, able to have a footprint everywhere, and so digital technology will continue to have a strong hold. The Central government or the State governments are also pushing very hard to go digital, follow the cashless transactions route. So, we have to move fast, to complete digitization, and a complete cashless transaction world.

Title: Credit bureaus and FinTechs should collaborate
Content:
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ap70gFKC25o" width="560" height="315" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe>

Pinkesh Ambavat, CIO, CRIF India informs how credit bureaus are leveraging on technology especially in the current situation.

Q. How do you see competition between credit bureaus and FinTech start-ups globally and also in India? How do you see the credit bureaus growing in Indian market?

Today, modern digital finance companies have adapted their own methods using alternative data sources to assess the creditworthiness of borrowers. But I do not see a competition happening globally, and not in India as well. I think there is a lot of collaboration happening because of the alternate data present with FinTech companies and financial transaction data present with the credit bureau. If they can be combined together a lot of innovation can happen or a lot of new products can be derived. For example, the credit bureau always faces an issue where the people who are very new to credit or who are taking credit for the first time, and it is very difficult to score them. With alternate data it will be very easy for them to score as well and take a decision whether to go to for credit or underwriting as well. I would say there is a lot of collaboration happening rather than competition.

It is a healthy collaboration because it is helping as in credit bureaus are seeing regular growth or the way market is growing credit bureau is also growing. But at the same time with this alternate data and FinTech startups coming into the picture, a lot of new products are also coming in the market. For example early salary, pay day, peer to peer lending those were not in the standard lending practices. These are the new concepts which are coming in because of the FinTechstartups. So there are also helping credit bureau to grow their business.

Q. Post COVID-19 where do you see their position in India’s banking system?

Post covid-19 situation their responsibility will increase in defining the landing strategy as well. Because now in the post covid-19 situation a lot of Indian households are in stress and credit decision is not going to be easy because of we have to identify who can really pay credit back. So creating a good lending strategy to avoid any defaults or NPAs in future is going to be a key. Credit bureau will also play a very important role in that.
Secondly collection is going to be very difficult in the post covid-19 situation as because of pandemic many people have lost their job. So creating early warnings on default, creating some collection solutions and that is how credit bureau is going to play an important role in the Indian banking system. Credit bureaus will do a lot of digital innovation and help banks to complete their lending solution digitally.

Q. What is the lesson security analyst or CISOs or CIOs should learn after this pandemic?  How is CRIF empowering its customers in this scenario?

We are already RBI licensed and before this pandemic we never thought of working from home. For the entire organisation this was a new normal and we also have to be ready for such kind of a situation. So the lesson learnt is that data security is the topmost priority for us. We have to make sure that all our data access has been secured. We need to also make sure that our infrastructure is capable enough to manage the workload for all the people who are working from home and that they are accessing all the data in a secured way. Most being RBI licenced and ISO certified, credit bureaus already have lot of things in place. So they were already prepared for this. Also customers are all the banks and financial institutions who are also RBI governed, and they are also dealing with all the financial data. So rather than we empowering them they are already aware of the securities, all the credit bureaus are already secured and so all the data is going through a secured channel.

Q. As a Risk Leader what is your top security concern post COVID-19? What are the lessons learned?

From the security point of view it is about making sure that end points where there are laptop and desktops are secured well because people are going to work from home because of the covid-19 situation and now this is going to be a new normal as well. So data leakage and endpoint protection are going to be our top most priority as well as protection against phishing emails. Phishing attack is going to be very important for us. The internal employee awareness is going to be very important and that is what we have learnt during covid-19 situation that whenever new people are joining a lot of phishing attacks are happening.

Q. What are the some challenges you have faced and how you have helped to build a strong cybersecurity framework?

The biggest challenge for us was that we never thought some of the production data will be accessed from home as we always accessed this data from a secure zone. So that was the biggest challenge of how to enable that. We have created some communication tool, managing the teamwork tool. There were challenges faced like how to track people's work, how to make sure that all the services are up and running and providing all the support from home, providing all the patching activities on a regular basis because during this pandemic situation we should not miss any patching activity. We have made sure that even if you are working from home all these things are taken care of and that is how we are building our cybersecurity as well.

Q. Post COVID-19 what would be the next big game-changer technology in FinTech according to you?

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are going to be big game changers. Guess now data is the new norm, so analytics around that and how you can cross sell your products, how you can scale your products and how you can identify some early warnings about defaults are going to be big game changers as well. Identifying the right kind of audience for your product is also important. Next is RPA. more process optimisation and improving operational efficiency are going to be big game changers. And how you can deploy your bot to automate your work .You must have seen a lot of chatbots are used by people to resolve customer queries and all.

Q. Please outline your growth roadmap post COVID-19. What will be the IT best practices in a post-COVID-19 world?

We are following a 50-30-20 budget tool for any IT investment or IT innovations which means that 50% will be to run the business coma, 30% will be foregoing the business and 20% will be for all the innovation or transformation from futuristic point of view. This is how we are doing from the last 5 years following the same practices. Credit bureaus are always doing a lot of innovations and we will continue to do that. But of course we have to reprioritize our business needs for this year because we have to really reduce our cost because of the pandemic situation. We will focus more on how we can reduce cost but at the same time we will continue how we can create some new business line or create new products for the next year.

Q. What is your vision for Risk Strategies in future, especially in FinTech? What would be your advice for the FinTech companies that are doing digital innovation?

We are going to collaborate with FinTech. It is not going to be a competition. Wherever we can collaborate and create new products that is going to be our strategy. I would advise FinTechs to create solutions keeping more customer in mind. Whatever they create, they should have four parameters in mind -- speed, simplicity, customer autonomy and distinct capability that are not part of a bundle service. Whatever they should create they should have customer focus.

Q. What would be your digital strategy for 2020 and beyond?

Credit bureau have already started working on digital strategy from the last couple of years because FinTechs have already started coming in from the last 4 years and to match the speed, credit bureaus are also doing a lot of innovation on the digital side and they are collaborating with them. So we are also going to do the same and we are going to invest into innovation, specially into artificial intelligence and machine learning, into RPA and Big Data. One strategy is also going to be how we can move to cloud and create some new products or analytics or some new score using these technologies.

Title: FSS Brings AutoPay and Conversational Capabilities to UPI
Content: Customers can set-up auto-debit instructions in a single click or by using voice commands FSS (Financial Software and Systems),a global digital payment and financial technology company, has augmented its UPI 2.0 platform with a range of new capabilities to improve customer convenience. This includes AutoPay and voice-activated account management to enable PSPs harness the potential of UPI, generate new monetization opportunities, and encourage frequent use of digital payments. Coinciding with the nation-wide launch by NPCI, two of the country’s leading banks were among the first to go live with FSS UPI AutoPay. Compliant with NPCI guidelines, FSS AutoPay unlocks new revenue opportunities for banks to collaborate with third party FinTechs for the development of new generation digital overlay services. This spans a broad range of services – consumer to business transactions (subscriptions and monthly payments ), business to consumer payments (‘buy now, pay later’ -- e-commerce initiatives) corporate pay-outs (payroll) and business-to-business payments (supply chain transactions). FSS UPI AutoPay allows customers (payers as well as payees) to set-up auto-debit instructions for regular payments using a mobile app or by scanning a QR code. All subsequent payments are seamlessly executed in the background, without any manual intervention, maximizing customer convenience. Using the PSP UPI app, customers can digitally set-up authorise, view, modify and manage mandates with a single click, ensuring visibility and control over these payment arrangements. With growing adoption of voice-based interfaces, FSS UPI 2.0 allows customers to manage their accounts using voice commands for an easy-to-use, on-the-go banking experience. Customers can use the conversational interface embedded in the UPI app to conduct a range of routine, non-financial transactions. This includes account creation and activation (create UPI id, create virtual private account), manage mandates, enquire balance, check transaction status (collect money), receive alerts (fund transfer status notification). The transactions are secured using data encryption and out-of-band authentication mechanisms such as a one-time password. Speaking on the launch of new capabilities, N Sathish, Deputy CPO FSS, stated; “The real-time payments landscape is evolving, and improved customer experience is at the heart of this transformation. Instantaneity and invisibility are the defining attributes of future consumer payment experiences. With AutoPay and conversational banking capabilities, FSS provides PSPs a compelling, new way to embed themselves deeper into their customers’ lives and further adoption of UPI-based payments.” The underlying FSS UPI Gateway supports standard secure interfaces for integration with third-party FinTechs and Voice Commerce systems. In addition, FSS UPI mobile SDK provides third party providers -- banks, fintech, retailers, telecoms, insurers, wallet providers – a quick out-of-the-box integration capability, enabling UPI services within the existing app in a few hours. FSS supports licensed and As-a-Service deployment models in line with PSP business needs. The solution is benchmarked to process 6,600 transactions per second and can scale to accommodate larger workloads.
